type IResourceOptions<T = unknown> = {
  debugName?: string
  ttl?: number // 默认 Infinity（永不过期，除非依赖变化/手动刷新）
  autoStart?: boolean // 默认 true
  staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean // 默认 false
  retry?: IResourceRetryPolicy // 默认 0（不重试）
  retryDelay?: number | ((failureCount: number, error: unknown) => number) // 默认 0
  keepAlive?: boolean // 默认 false
  initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>
  scheduler?: IScheduler // 默认 @migaia/utils/scheduler 的 systemScheduler
}

type IResourceRetryPolicy = number | ((failureCount: number, error: unknown) => boolean)

blocks.text: 逐项语义与校验：

items: `ttl?: number` —— 成功值的新鲜时长（毫秒）。`0` 与 `Infinity`（默认）表示永不因时间过期，只会因依赖变化/`refetch()`/`invalidate()` 而刷新。非 `Infinity` 时必须是有限非负数，否则抛贴 `INVALID_OPTION` 码的 `RangeError`；`updatedAt + ttl` 运算结果非有限（数值溢出）同样抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。
`autoStart?: boolean` —— 是否在构造函数内立即发起首次请求。默认 `true`。若同时提供了新鲜的 `initialSnapshot`，即使 `autoStart: true` 也不会立即再发一次请求。
`staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`。为 `true` 时，刷新期间继续展示旧的 `success` 数据（附带 `refreshing: true`），而不是回退到 `pending`。

`retry?: number | (failureCount, error) => boolean` —— 固定次数或自定义判断函数。数字必须是非负整数，否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。函数形式在每次失败后被调用一次，用第几次失败（从 1 开始）与错误对象决定是否重试；Suspense 抛出的 thenable 值不计入失败次数（`fetcher` 内部同步抛出一个 thenable 是被当作"需要等待后重跑"处理的，不是一次真实失败）。

`retryDelay?: number | (failureCount, error) => number` —— 固定延迟或按失败次数计算的函数，单位毫秒。数字必须是有限非负数；函数返回非数字时以原生 `TypeError`/`INVALID_OPTION` 拒绝；返回负数/非有限数字则为 `RangeError`/`INVALID_OPTION`。策略抛错或返回非法值时保留触发重试的 fetch 主因，原生策略 Error 尽量原样附码，已有外部身份不改写。
`keepAlive?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`：长时间无人观察 `state` 会在下一个 idle 时机自动休眠（断开上游边、保留依赖版本与缓存），下次读取核对版本；依赖未变且缓存新鲜时继续复用，变更时重拉。设为 `true` 时禁用自动休眠。
`initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>` —— SSR/持久化恢复用的初始成功快照；构造期即 `hydrate()`，格式非法抛 `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`（详见快照类型）。

`scheduler?: IScheduler`（`@migaia/utils/scheduler`）—— 时间域与排程来源：TTL/`updatedAt`/`expiresAt`/重试延迟全部走同一个调度器，默认 `@migaia/utils/scheduler` 的 `systemScheduler`（单调时钟）。传入的值必须满足 `{ now(): number; schedule(cb, delayMs): IScheduledTask }` 契约（内部用 `snapshotScheduler` 校验），否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`；缺宿主能力时该 scheduler 在被调用时才 fail-fast，不会静默降级成微任务。

symbols.name: Resource
symbols.purpose: Creates one async data source bound to a reactive runtime. Every request gets a generation; only the result of the newest generation is written to `state`, and replaced requests receive an aborted `signal`. With `autoStart` (default) the first request starts in the constructor unless `initialSnapshot` is fresh.
symbols.core:
fetcher: Function `(context) => value | Promise` that loads the data. `context` comes from the resource for each request: `signal` aborts when the request is replaced, reset, cancelled or disposed; `generation` is the request number; `token` stays the same across retries of one request. Reactive values read synchronously (before the first `await`) become dependencies. Final unclassified fetch failures receive `FETCH_FAILED`; existing external error identity stays intact, and immutable errors or primitive failures remain reachable through `cause`.
runtime: Reactive runtime returned by `createRuntime()` from `@migaia/reactive`; the same runtime must own the signals the fetcher reads and the effects that read `state`. `dispose()` does not dispose it.
A `Resource` instance; invalid options throw `INVALID_OPTION`, an invalid `initialSnapshot` throws `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`.
deps: Reactive values the last request read synchronously; a change in any of them schedules a new request. Read-only, for diagnostics.
depVersions: Version of each dependency seen by the last request, used by the reactive runtime to skip refreshes when nothing really changed.
runtime: The runtime passed to the constructor; the resource registers itself there as an observer.
debugName: Label given by the `debugName` option, shown in reactive diagnostics and request error context.
state: Current state as a reactive read: an effect that reads it reruns when the state changes. Reading an expired success value starts a revalidation. Throws `RESOURCE_DISPOSED` after `dispose()`.
promise: Promise of the current request, or a resolved Promise of a fresh cached value. Readers share the latest published request Promise; a reentrant fetcher cannot overwrite a Promise of a newer request. Reading it starts work only when idle or stale.
disposed: `true` after `dispose()`; still readable afterwards, unlike most members.
refreshing: `true` while a background refresh runs and the previous success data stays visible (`staleWhileRevalidate`).
fetchStatus: `fetching` while any request runs, otherwise `idle`; separate from `state.status`.
isStale: `true` when the cached success value is older than `ttl`; `false` for any other state.
observed: `true` while some effect or computed currently reads `state`; without observers and without `keepAlive` the resource drops its upstream dependencies.
read: Suspense-style read with tracking: returns the data on success, throws the pending Promise while loading, and throws the error after failure or cancellation.
The data of the current success state.
peek: Materializes the current state without tracking, starting work or revalidating TTL. Pending throws its Promise; normal `autoStart: false` idle with no Promise throws `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`. Inspect `peekState()` or explicitly start work first.
peekState: Returns the state without tracking, without starting work and without checking `ttl`.
An `IResourceState` snapshot: branch on `status` (`idle`, `pending`, `success` with `data`, `error` / `cancelled` with `error`).
reset: Cancels the running request, drops cached data and returns to `idle`; the next read starts again.
Nothing; the state is now `idle`.
refetch: Starts a new request even if the cache is fresh, aborting the running one.
Promise of the new request result.
invalidate: Marks the cached data as expired and starts a replacement request at once.
Promise of the replacement request result.
cancel: With an active request, aborts it and pauses passive restarts. Pending becomes `cancelled` (`REQUEST_CANCELLED`); a stale-while-revalidate refresh keeps its success data. Without active work this is a no-op; explicit `refetch()` resumes work.
Nothing; active work is cancelled while cached success data may remain.
dehydrate: Captures a v2 success snapshot with portable durations and unchanged caller-owned data. Only time metadata is directly JSON-encodable: BigInt or cyclic data needs caller serialization. Use safe transport or HTML-context encoding; never insert raw JSON into a script element.
An `IResourceCacheSnapshot`, or `undefined` when the state is not `success`.
hydrate: Replaces the state with a success snapshot produced by `dehydrate()`, cancelling any running request. An expired snapshot is revalidated on the next read. Durations are rebased to the receiving scheduler; callers add known transport/storage time to `ageMs` and subtract it from finite `remainingTtlMs` (minimum zero). Old v1 snapshots are rejected.
hydrate.snapshot: Snapshot returned by `dehydrate()` (often on the server); malformed snapshots throw `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`.
Nothing; the state is now `success`.
markDirty: The reactive runtime calls this when a value read by the Resource request changes. It schedules a refresh and groups repeated notifications into that scheduled refresh. Application code changes the input, such as userId.value, and lets the runtime send this notification; it does not need to call markDirty().
Nothing; a refresh is scheduled.
onDependencyDisconnected: The reactive runtime calls this when an input used by the Resource has been disposed and can no longer supply a value. It schedules another request even without an ordinary input change. If that request fails while reading the disposed input, the failure becomes visible in the Resource error state. Application code disposes the input and lets the runtime call this method.
Nothing; a forced refresh is scheduled.
mutate: Replaces the visible data locally (optimistic update, server push, cache write). Any in-flight request is superseded so its late result cannot overwrite this value, and a new TTL window starts. An updater receives the current success data or `undefined`; function-typed data must be passed through an updater.
mutate.next: New data, or an `IResourceUpdater` `(previous) => next`; an updater throw leaves the state unchanged.
This resource, for chaining; after `dispose()` it throws `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`.
subscribe: Delivers the current state now and after every change to code that does not run inside the reactive graph (plain scripts, devtools, Node). Subscribing counts as observation, so it can start and keep requests alive. Listener throws are reported through `runtime.reportError` and do not stop delivery.
subscribe.listener: Function `(state) => void` receiving each `IResourceState`; a non-function throws `INVALID_OPTION`.
An idempotent unsubscribe function; `dispose()` unsubscribes automatically.
select: Creates a reactive value derived from the success data; it is `undefined` while the resource is not in `success`, and it is disposed together with the resource.
select.selector: Function `(data) => result`; a non-function throws `INVALID_OPTION`.
An `IReactiveComputed` from `@migaia/reactive`; read it through `value` inside effects.
[Symbol.dispose]: Same as `dispose()`, so a `using` declaration ends the resource when its block exits.
Nothing; the resource is terminal.
dispose: Ends the resource: cancels the request, removes dependencies and subscriptions. Calling it again does nothing; afterwards data reads and operations throw `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`, while `disposed`, `refreshing` and `observed` stay readable. The runtime is not disposed.
debugName: Label shown in reactive diagnostics and in request error context.
Not set: diagnostics show no label.
ttl: Success lifetime in milliseconds; positive finite lifetimes revalidate on an expired read. `0` and `Infinity` disable time expiration, but changed dependencies, including after suspension, still trigger refetching. Must be ≥ 0 or `Infinity`.
`Infinity`: fresh until a dependency changes or `refetch()` is called.
autoStart: Start the first request in the constructor.
`true`: starts immediately unless the initial snapshot is fresh.
staleWhileRevalidate: Keep showing expired success data while the refresh runs (`refreshing` is `true`) instead of switching to `pending`.
`false`: an expired value is replaced by `pending`.
retry: Retry policy after a failure: a non-negative integer of extra attempts, or `(failureCount, error) => boolean` deciding each retry. A Promise thrown for Suspense does not count as a failure. A throwing policy or invalid result yields `INVALID_OPTION`; the triggering fetch failure stays reachable through `cause` or `errors`, and existing external identity is preserved.
`0`: no retry.
retryDelay: Wait before each retry in milliseconds, or `(failureCount, error) => ms` for backoff. Throwing callbacks or invalid results retain the fetch failure in `cause` or `errors`; policy errors receive `INVALID_OPTION` unless already classified externally.
`0`: retry immediately.
Pass a function when the server is overloaded or rate limited: immediate retries add load at the worst moment. `failureCount` starts at 1, so `1000 * 2 ** (failureCount - 1)` waits 1 s, 2 s, 4 s. You can also read `error` and wait longer for a 429 than for a network error. A plain number is enough when failures are short network blips.
keepAlive: Keep upstream dependencies connected while nothing reads `state`, so changes are still tracked.
`false`: unobserved resources disconnect upstream.
initialSnapshot: Success snapshot from `dehydrate()` (server rendering or persistence) used as the initial state; it is revalidated when expired.
Not set: start from `idle`.
scheduler: Clock and timers for `ttl`, `updatedAt`, `expiresAt` and retry delays; inject a manual scheduler in tests.
`systemScheduler` from `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
symbols.advanced:
Load data that depends on reactive inputs (user id, filters): changing an input cancels the old request and starts a new one, and an old answer can never overwrite the new state.
Feed React Suspense and error boundaries through `read()`.
Cache with a lifetime (`ttl`), keep showing old data while refreshing (`staleWhileRevalidate`), and restore server-rendered data with `dehydrate()` / `hydrate()`.
One-off loads without inputs, cancellation, retry or expiry (for example static config at startup): a plain `await` is simpler.
parameters: fetcher: IResourceFetcher<T>
runtime: IRuntime
options: IResourceOptions<T> (optional)

import { createRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'
import { Resource } from '@migaia/resource'

const value = new Resource(({ generation }) => generation, createRuntime(), { autoStart: false })
console.log(value.peekState().status) // idle：请求函数还没被调用
console.log(await value.promise)
value.reset()
console.log(value.peekState().status) // idle：同一个实例，没有缓存数据

value.dispose()

members.description: Force a new request. Explicit refetches do not reuse a fresh cache entry; passive `promise`/`read()` consumers do.

Supersedes any in-flight request so its late result cannot overwrite this value, and starts a fresh TTL window. An updater receives the current success data (or `undefined`). Function-typed data must be passed through an updater. Returns `this` for chaining. ;```ts todos.mutate((list = []) => [...list, draft]) ```

symbols.whenToUse:
Load data that depends on reactive inputs (user id, filters): changing an input cancels the old request and starts a new one, and an old answer can never overwrite the new state.
Feed React Suspense and error boundaries through `read()`.
Cache with a lifetime (`ttl`), keep showing old data while refreshing (`staleWhileRevalidate`), and restore server-rendered data with `dehydrate()` / `hydrate()`.
symbols.notUse: One-off loads without inputs, cancellation, retry or expiry (for example static config at startup): a plain `await` is simpler.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Creates one async data source bound to a reactive runtime. Every request gets a generation; only the result of the newest generation is written to `state`, and replaced requests receive an aborted `signal`. With `autoStart` (default) the first request starts in the constructor unless `initialSnapshot` is fresh.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import Resource from @migaia/resource, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use Resource when its class contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when Resource does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained class example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
fetcher: Function `(context) => value | Promise` that loads the data. `context` comes from the resource for each request: `signal` aborts when the request is replaced, reset, cancelled or disposed; `generation` is the request number; `token` stays the same across retries of one request. Reactive values read synchronously (before the first `await`) become dependencies. Final unclassified fetch failures receive `FETCH_FAILED`; existing external error identity stays intact, and immutable errors or primitive failures remain reachable through `cause`.
runtime: Reactive runtime returned by `createRuntime()` from `@migaia/reactive`; the same runtime must own the signals the fetcher reads and the effects that read `state`. `dispose()` does not dispose it.
A `Resource` instance; invalid options throw `INVALID_OPTION`, an invalid `initialSnapshot` throws `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`.
deps: Reactive values the last request read synchronously; a change in any of them schedules a new request. Read-only, for diagnostics.
depVersions: Version of each dependency seen by the last request, used by the reactive runtime to skip refreshes when nothing really changed.
runtime: The runtime passed to the constructor; the resource registers itself there as an observer.
debugName: Label given by the `debugName` option, shown in reactive diagnostics and request error context.
state: Current state as a reactive read: an effect that reads it reruns when the state changes. Reading an expired success value starts a revalidation. Throws `RESOURCE_DISPOSED` after `dispose()`.
promise: Promise of the current request, or a resolved Promise of a fresh cached value. Readers share the latest published request Promise; a reentrant fetcher cannot overwrite a Promise of a newer request. Reading it starts work only when idle or stale.
disposed: `true` after `dispose()`; still readable afterwards, unlike most members.
refreshing: `true` while a background refresh runs and the previous success data stays visible (`staleWhileRevalidate`).
fetchStatus: `fetching` while any request runs, otherwise `idle`; separate from `state.status`.
isStale: `true` when the cached success value is older than `ttl`; `false` for any other state.
observed: `true` while some effect or computed currently reads `state`; without observers and without `keepAlive` the resource drops its upstream dependencies.
read: Suspense-style read with tracking: returns the data on success, throws the pending Promise while loading, and throws the error after failure or cancellation.
The data of the current success state.
peek: Materializes the current state without tracking, starting work or revalidating TTL. Pending throws its Promise; normal `autoStart: false` idle with no Promise throws `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`. Inspect `peekState()` or explicitly start work first.
peekState: Returns the state without tracking, without starting work and without checking `ttl`.
An `IResourceState` snapshot: branch on `status` (`idle`, `pending`, `success` with `data`, `error` / `cancelled` with `error`).
reset: Cancels the running request, drops cached data and returns to `idle`; the next read starts again.
Nothing; the state is now `idle`.
refetch: Starts a new request even if the cache is fresh, aborting the running one.
Promise of the new request result.
invalidate: Marks the cached data as expired and starts a replacement request at once.
Promise of the replacement request result.
cancel: With an active request, aborts it and pauses passive restarts. Pending becomes `cancelled` (`REQUEST_CANCELLED`); a stale-while-revalidate refresh keeps its success data. Without active work this is a no-op; explicit `refetch()` resumes work.
Nothing; active work is cancelled while cached success data may remain.
dehydrate: Captures a v2 success snapshot with portable durations and unchanged caller-owned data. Only time metadata is directly JSON-encodable: BigInt or cyclic data needs caller serialization. Use safe transport or HTML-context encoding; never insert raw JSON into a script element.
An `IResourceCacheSnapshot`, or `undefined` when the state is not `success`.
hydrate: Replaces the state with a success snapshot produced by `dehydrate()`, cancelling any running request. An expired snapshot is revalidated on the next read. Durations are rebased to the receiving scheduler; callers add known transport/storage time to `ageMs` and subtract it from finite `remainingTtlMs` (minimum zero). Old v1 snapshots are rejected.
hydrate.snapshot: Snapshot returned by `dehydrate()` (often on the server); malformed snapshots throw `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`.
Nothing; the state is now `success`.
markDirty: The reactive runtime calls this when a value read by the Resource request changes. It schedules a refresh and groups repeated notifications into that scheduled refresh. Application code changes the input, such as userId.value, and lets the runtime send this notification; it does not need to call markDirty().
Nothing; a refresh is scheduled.
onDependencyDisconnected: The reactive runtime calls this when an input used by the Resource has been disposed and can no longer supply a value. It schedules another request even without an ordinary input change. If that request fails while reading the disposed input, the failure becomes visible in the Resource error state. Application code disposes the input and lets the runtime call this method.
Nothing; a forced refresh is scheduled.
mutate: Replaces the visible data locally (optimistic update, server push, cache write). Any in-flight request is superseded so its late result cannot overwrite this value, and a new TTL window starts. An updater receives the current success data or `undefined`; function-typed data must be passed through an updater.
mutate.next: New data, or an `IResourceUpdater` `(previous) => next`; an updater throw leaves the state unchanged.
This resource, for chaining; after `dispose()` it throws `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`.
subscribe: Delivers the current state now and after every change to code that does not run inside the reactive graph (plain scripts, devtools, Node). Subscribing counts as observation, so it can start and keep requests alive. Listener throws are reported through `runtime.reportError` and do not stop delivery.
subscribe.listener: Function `(state) => void` receiving each `IResourceState`; a non-function throws `INVALID_OPTION`.
An idempotent unsubscribe function; `dispose()` unsubscribes automatically.
select: Creates a reactive value derived from the success data; it is `undefined` while the resource is not in `success`, and it is disposed together with the resource.
select.selector: Function `(data) => result`; a non-function throws `INVALID_OPTION`.
An `IReactiveComputed` from `@migaia/reactive`; read it through `value` inside effects.
[Symbol.dispose]: Same as `dispose()`, so a `using` declaration ends the resource when its block exits.
Nothing; the resource is terminal.
dispose: Ends the resource: cancels the request, removes dependencies and subscriptions. Calling it again does nothing; afterwards data reads and operations throw `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`, while `disposed`, `refreshing` and `observed` stay readable. The runtime is not disposed.
debugName: Label shown in reactive diagnostics and in request error context.
Not set: diagnostics show no label.
ttl: Success lifetime in milliseconds; positive finite lifetimes revalidate on an expired read. `0` and `Infinity` disable time expiration, but changed dependencies, including after suspension, still trigger refetching. Must be ≥ 0 or `Infinity`.
`Infinity`: fresh until a dependency changes or `refetch()` is called.
autoStart: Start the first request in the constructor.
`true`: starts immediately unless the initial snapshot is fresh.
staleWhileRevalidate: Keep showing expired success data while the refresh runs (`refreshing` is `true`) instead of switching to `pending`.
`false`: an expired value is replaced by `pending`.
retry: Retry policy after a failure: a non-negative integer of extra attempts, or `(failureCount, error) => boolean` deciding each retry. A Promise thrown for Suspense does not count as a failure. A throwing policy or invalid result yields `INVALID_OPTION`; the triggering fetch failure stays reachable through `cause` or `errors`, and existing external identity is preserved.
`0`: no retry.
retryDelay: Wait before each retry in milliseconds, or `(failureCount, error) => ms` for backoff. Throwing callbacks or invalid results retain the fetch failure in `cause` or `errors`; policy errors receive `INVALID_OPTION` unless already classified externally.
`0`: retry immediately.
Pass a function when the server is overloaded or rate limited: immediate retries add load at the worst moment. `failureCount` starts at 1, so `1000 * 2 ** (failureCount - 1)` waits 1 s, 2 s, 4 s. You can also read `error` and wait longer for a 429 than for a network error. A plain number is enough when failures are short network blips.
keepAlive: Keep upstream dependencies connected while nothing reads `state`, so changes are still tracked.
`false`: unobserved resources disconnect upstream.
initialSnapshot: Success snapshot from `dehydrate()` (server rendering or persistence) used as the initial state; it is revalidated when expired.
Not set: start from `idle`.
scheduler: Clock and timers for `ttl`, `updatedAt`, `expiresAt` and retry delays; inject a manual scheduler in tests.
`systemScheduler` from `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.

sections.title: 高阶用法
sections.content:
Load data that depends on reactive inputs (user id, filters): changing an input cancels the old request and starts a new one, and an old answer can never overwrite the new state.
Feed React Suspense and error boundaries through `read()`.
Cache with a lifetime (`ttl`), keep showing old data while refreshing (`staleWhileRevalidate`), and restore server-rendered data with `dehydrate()` / `hydrate()`.
One-off loads without inputs, cancellation, retry or expiry (for example static config at startup): a plain `await` is simpler.

declaredConfiguration.name: debugName
declaredConfiguration.description: Human-readable owner label used in reactive diagnostics and request error context.

declaredConfiguration.name: ttl
declaredConfiguration.description: Successful values remain fresh for this many milliseconds. `0` and `Infinity` keep them fresh until a dependency changes or `refetch()` is called.

declaredConfiguration.name: autoStart
declaredConfiguration.description: Start the first request in the constructor. Defaults to true.

declaredConfiguration.name: staleWhileRevalidate
declaredConfiguration.description: Keep stale success data visible while a background refresh runs.

declaredConfiguration.name: retry
declaredConfiguration.description: Retry count or predicate. Suspense Promise throws do not count.

declaredConfiguration.name: retryDelay
declaredConfiguration.description: Milliseconds to wait before the next retry, fixed or computed from the failure number and error. Defaults to 0.

declaredConfiguration.name: keepAlive
declaredConfiguration.description: Keep upstream reactive edges while no state consumer exists.

declaredConfiguration.name: initialSnapshot
declaredConfiguration.description: SSR/persisted success cache used before optional revalidation.

declaredConfiguration.name: scheduler
declaredConfiguration.description: Supplies one scheduler for TTL, `updatedAt`, `expiresAt`, and retry delays. Defaults to utils/scheduler `systemScheduler`. Missing host capabilities fail immediately instead of silently falling back to microtasks.

guidance.id: 取消后显示已取消而不是错误
guidance.heading: 取消后显示已取消而不是错误

blocks.text: 用户点了“取消导出”，界面却弹出“导出失败”，因为取消和失败走进了同一个 `catch`。
手写的状态通常只有“加载中、成功、失败”三种，取消只能塞进“失败”，再靠比较错误信息字符串来区分。
`cancel()` 把还在等待的请求变成 `cancelled` 状态，`state.error` 是原生 `AbortError`。资源本身没有被释放，之后调用 `refetch()` 可以重新开始。
输出：

blocks.code:
状态：cancelled
原因：AbortError
第 2 次导出完成

blocks.text: 取消后状态是 `cancelled`，原因是 `AbortError`；随后 `refetch()` 正常完成，输出“第 2 次导出完成”。
`cancelled` 是单独的状态，界面可以按 `ResourceStatus.cancelled` 显示“已取消”。取消后再读取 `state` 不会自动重启请求，只有显式调用 `refetch()` 才会。

函数式构建 `Resource`。`setup` 只同步执行一次，拿到 `{ runtime, scheduler, signal, debugName, onDispose }`，返回 fetcher；数据类型从 fetcher 推导。`options` 就是 `IResourceOptions` 加上可选的 `runtime`（默认 `@migaia/reactive` 的 `defaultRuntime`）。

items: `onDispose` 注册的清理在 `dispose()` 时按注册的逆序执行，`signal` 同时中止。
`setup` 抛错、返回值不是函数（`RESOURCE_SETUP_INVALID`）或选项非法时，先中止 `signal`、逆序执行已注册清理，再重抛原始错误；清理失败挂在 `errors` 上。
`setup` 返回后再调用 `onDispose` 会抛 `RESOURCE_SETUP_CLOSED`，避免泄漏。

blocks.text: 配合 `ConfigOwner.fromAsync` 得到配置资源：

blocks.code:
type IResourceOptions<T = unknown> = {
  debugName?: string
  ttl?: number // 默认 Infinity（永不过期，除非依赖变化/手动刷新）
  autoStart?: boolean // 默认 true
  staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean // 默认 false
  retry?: IResourceRetryPolicy // 默认 0（不重试）
  retryDelay?: number | ((failureCount: number, error: unknown) => number) // 默认 0
  keepAlive?: boolean // 默认 false
  initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>
  scheduler?: IScheduler // 默认 @migaia/utils/scheduler 的 systemScheduler
}

type IResourceRetryPolicy = number | ((failureCount: number, error: unknown) => boolean)

blocks.text: 逐项语义与校验：

items: `ttl?: number` —— 成功值的新鲜时长（毫秒）。`0` 与 `Infinity`（默认）表示永不因时间过期，只会因依赖变化/`refetch()`/`invalidate()` 而刷新。非 `Infinity` 时必须是有限非负数，否则抛贴 `INVALID_OPTION` 码的 `RangeError`；`updatedAt + ttl` 运算结果非有限（数值溢出）同样抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。
`autoStart?: boolean` —— 是否在构造函数内立即发起首次请求。默认 `true`。若同时提供了新鲜的 `initialSnapshot`，即使 `autoStart: true` 也不会立即再发一次请求。
`staleWhileRevalidate?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`。为 `true` 时，刷新期间继续展示旧的 `success` 数据（附带 `refreshing: true`），而不是回退到 `pending`。

`retry?: number | (failureCount, error) => boolean` —— 固定次数或自定义判断函数。数字必须是非负整数，否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`。函数形式在每次失败后被调用一次，用第几次失败（从 1 开始）与错误对象决定是否重试；Suspense 抛出的 thenable 值不计入失败次数（`fetcher` 内部同步抛出一个 thenable 是被当作"需要等待后重跑"处理的，不是一次真实失败）。

`retryDelay?: number | (failureCount, error) => number` —— 固定延迟或按失败次数计算的函数，单位毫秒。数字必须是有限非负数；函数返回非数字时以原生 `TypeError`/`INVALID_OPTION` 拒绝；返回负数/非有限数字则为 `RangeError`/`INVALID_OPTION`。策略抛错或返回非法值时保留触发重试的 fetch 主因，原生策略 Error 尽量原样附码，已有外部身份不改写。
`keepAlive?: boolean` —— 默认 `false`：长时间无人观察 `state` 会在下一个 idle 时机自动休眠（断开上游边、保留依赖版本与缓存），下次读取核对版本；依赖未变且缓存新鲜时继续复用，变更时重拉。设为 `true` 时禁用自动休眠。
`initialSnapshot?: IResourceCacheSnapshot<T>` —— SSR/持久化恢复用的初始成功快照；构造期即 `hydrate()`，格式非法抛 `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`（详见快照类型）。

`scheduler?: IScheduler`（`@migaia/utils/scheduler`）—— 时间域与排程来源：TTL/`updatedAt`/`expiresAt`/重试延迟全部走同一个调度器，默认 `@migaia/utils/scheduler` 的 `systemScheduler`（单调时钟）。传入的值必须满足 `{ now(): number; schedule(cb, delayMs): IScheduledTask }` 契约（内部用 `snapshotScheduler` 校验），否则抛 `INVALID_OPTION`；缺宿主能力时该 scheduler 在被调用时才 fail-fast，不会静默降级成微任务。

guidance.id: 底层依赖-lifecycle-原语的使用方式
guidance.heading: 底层依赖：lifecycle 原语的使用方式

blocks.text: `Resource` 内部直接组合 `@migaia/lifecycle` 与 `@migaia/reactive` 的原语，理解这层有助于诊断边界行为：

items: `createGenerationController()`（来自 `@migaia/lifecycle`）——每次发起请求都调用 `begin()` 开一代新请求；`refetch()`/`invalidate()`/依赖变化都会使旧一代失效（`supersede()`），只有 `isCurrent(token)` 为真的那一代结果才会写入 `state`。`dispose()` 时调用其 `dispose()` 终结控制器。
`createTerminalController()`（来自 `@migaia/lifecycle`）——驱动 `Resource` 自身的容器存活轴（`open → closing → terminal`）；`disposed` getter 直接读它的 `lifecycle === 'terminal'`。
`probeThenable()` / `assimilateCapturedThen()`（来自 `@migaia/utils/function`）——用于安全探测 `fetcher` 同步抛出的值是否是 thenable（Suspense 抛 Promise 模式），只读一次 `.then`，避免 hostile getter 被读取两次或异常被吞掉。
`systemScheduler`（来自 `@migaia/utils/scheduler`）/ `snapshotScheduler()`（来自 `@migaia/lifecycle`）——`scheduler` 选项的默认值与校验函数；TTL 到期判定、重试延迟计时都通过它，不直接使用宿主 `setTimeout`/`Date.now`。
`internalRuntimeOf()` / `createTrackedObserver()`（来自 `@migaia/reactive/extension`）——Resource作为IObserver接入图，仅获得绑定自身的追踪、挂起、重验证与idle能力；依赖集合由reactive内部维护，请求、取消与资源释放仍由Resource负责。

guidance.id: 高阶组合示例-1-suspense-兼容读取-error-boundary
guidance.heading: 高阶组合示例 · 1. Suspense 兼容读取 + Error Boundary

blocks.text: 构造选项 `autoStart` 默认为 `true`：没有仍有效的 `initialSnapshot` 时，构造函数立即发起第一代请求。传 `autoStart: false` 时不在构造期请求，首次被动读取仍可启动；有效的初始快照会直接复用。

1. 依赖追踪只认第一个 `await` 之前的同步读取。 `await` 之后再读响应式值不会被追踪；需要时先把值读进局部变量，或者把读取挪进一个 `Computed`。依赖变化何时刷新由传入的 `runtime` 调度决定，默认在微任务中处理。 2. 请求函数要把 `signal` 交给真正可取消的 I/O（例如 `fetch(url, { signal })`）。否则取消只是让 `Resource` 忽略这次结果，底层请求仍会跑完。 3. `refetch()` 总是发起新请求；被动读取（`state`、`promise`、`read()`）只在 `idle` 或数据过期时才发起。 每次刷新会创建新的一代，并中止仍在途的上一代的 `signal`；只有当前一代能把结果写入状态。想强制刷新就调用 `refetch()` 或 `invalidate()`。 4. 不再使用时要调用 `dispose()`，否则依赖登记和进行中的请求会一直留着。释放后读取数据和发起请求都抛 `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`；`disposed`、`refreshing`、`observed` 仍可读，`markDirty()`、`onDependencyDisconnected()` 和再次 `dispose()` 是安全的空操作。`dispose()` 不会释放传入的 `runtime`。 5. 默认 `keepAlive: false`。 没人读取 `state` 时，`Resource` 会和上游断开但保留依赖版本与缓存；下次读取时依赖没变且缓存有效就复用原值和 Promise，依赖变了就重新请求。需要“没人看也保持连接”时传 `keepAlive: true`。 6. `cancel()` 之后被动读取不会自动重启。 需要暂时停止当前请求、稍后继续使用同一个资源时调用 `cancel()`。正在加载的请求被取消后状态是 `cancelled`；后台刷新被取消时保留旧数据并清除 `refreshing`。只有显式 `refetch()` 会重新开始。

`Resource` 自己产生的错误带 `source === RESOURCE_SOURCE`（`resource`）和 `ResourceErrorCode` 里的 `code`。已经有完整 `source`/`code` 的外部错误保持原样；没有分类的加载失败在重试结束后附加 `FETCH_FAILED`，原生错误保持原类型，不可修改的错误保留在 `cause` 链上。重试策略本身出错时附加 `INVALID_OPTION`，触发它的加载错误仍可从错误链找到。取消和释放产生的错误是原生 `DOMException`（`name === 'AbortError'`），按 `error.name` 判断即可。

configuration.name: ttl

configuration.name: autoStart

configuration.name: retry

configuration.description: `dehydrate()` 导出数据和两个时长：已经存在了多久（`ageMs`）、还能有效多久（`remainingTtlMs`）。浏览器把它作为 `initialSnapshot` 传入，`Resource` 用本地时钟接着计时，快照仍有效时不发请求。
configuration.descriptionEn: SSR/persisted success cache used before optional revalidation.

symbols.name: ResourceErrorCode
symbols.purpose: Table of the stable error codes of this package. Each key names one failure; the values are the strings found on `error.code`.
symbols.core:
resourceDisposed: `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`: a member was used after `dispose()`; create a new resource.
requestAborted: `REQUEST_ABORTED`: Resource-initiated cancellation uses the same native AbortError as its signal reason and rejection. Lifecycle replacement can supply a different signal reason, retained on the `cause` of the Resource AbortError.
requestCancelled: `REQUEST_CANCELLED`: the `AbortError` stored in the `cancelled` state after `cancel()`.
cancellationCleanupFailed: `CANCELLATION_CLEANUP_FAILED`: a timer or listener could not be cleaned after cancellation; the resource still counts as cancelled.
noActivePromise: `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`: no request Promise is available, including a valid `autoStart: false` idle `peek()`; inspect `peekState()` or explicitly start a request.
invalidSnapshot: `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`: snapshot version is not `2`, durations are negative/non-finite (only remaining lifetime permits `null`), or rebased local timestamps overflow. Getter failures retain their cause.
invalidOption: `INVALID_OPTION`: an option such as `ttl`, `retry` or `retryDelay` is invalid; fix the options.
fetchFailed: `FETCH_FAILED`: final unclassified fetch failure after retries. Native errors keep identity when writable; immutable errors and primitive values stay reachable through `cause`. Existing foreign source/code is preserved.
setupInvalid: `RESOURCE_SETUP_INVALID`: `createResource()` got a non-function setup, or setup returned a non-function; registered cleanups already ran. Return a fetcher from setup.
setupClosed: `RESOURCE_SETUP_CLOSED`: `onDispose()` was called after setup returned, for example from an async callback; register cleanups synchronously during setup.
suspenseProbeFailed: `SUSPENSE_PROBE_FAILED`: a value thrown by the fetcher has a throwing `then` getter; both errors are kept in `errors`.

members.name: resourceDisposed
members.description: Rejects operations guarded by `#assertUsable()` after the `Resource` is disposed. This prevents * reading stale state after tracking stops. Repeated `dispose()` remains a no-op, and lifecycle * inspection getters remain available. Use a new `Resource` for further data reads or * operations.

members.name: requestAborted
members.description: Identifies the native AbortError for a stopped request. Resource-initiated cancellation uses * this same error as signal.reason; lifecycle-owned replacement reasons remain on its cause. * Callers usually recognize `error.name === 'AbortError'` and handle cancellation quietly.

members.name: requestCancelled
members.description: Identifies the `DOMException` in the `cancelled` state when explicit `cancel()` cancels a * pending request. Preserves the native `AbortError` type. Unlike `REQUEST_ABORTED`, which * identifies request rejection, this code identifies explicit cancellation state.

members.name: cancellationCleanupFailed
members.description: Reports timer or listener cleanup failure after request cancellation converges state. * `REQUEST_CANCELLED` identifies the `AbortError` stored in the cancelled state. This code * separates cleanup failures from state errors. Record the cleanup failure and continue treating * the `Resource` as cancelled.

members.name: noActivePromise
members.description: Reports a missing active or cached Promise when reading `promise` or materializing `pending` or * `idle`. This usually indicates inconsistent intermediate state. Check for internal state * changes that bypass the normal `refetch()` or `invalidate()` paths.

members.name: invalidSnapshot
members.description: Rejects a version other than 2, negative/nonfinite age or remaining lifetime, or durations that * cannot be rebased into finite local scheduler timestamps. Accessor failures retain their cause. * `remainingTtlMs: null` means unbounded lifetime. Migrate old absolute-time snapshots * explicitly; their sender clock origin cannot be inferred on the receiver.

members.name: invalidOption
members.description: Rejects construction or operation options such as invalid `ttl`, retry counts, or `retryDelay`. * Validation rejects invalid configuration before it enters the state machine. sections.content: Table of the stable error codes of this package. Each key names one failure; the values are the strings found on `error.code`.

sections.title: 上手

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
resourceDisposed: `RESOURCE_DISPOSED`: a member was used after `dispose()`; create a new resource.
requestAborted: `REQUEST_ABORTED`: Resource-initiated cancellation uses the same native AbortError as its signal reason and rejection. Lifecycle replacement can supply a different signal reason, retained on the `cause` of the Resource AbortError.
requestCancelled: `REQUEST_CANCELLED`: the `AbortError` stored in the `cancelled` state after `cancel()`.
cancellationCleanupFailed: `CANCELLATION_CLEANUP_FAILED`: a timer or listener could not be cleaned after cancellation; the resource still counts as cancelled.
noActivePromise: `NO_ACTIVE_PROMISE`: no request Promise is available, including a valid `autoStart: false` idle `peek()`; inspect `peekState()` or explicitly start a request.
invalidSnapshot: `INVALID_SNAPSHOT`: snapshot version is not `2`, durations are negative/non-finite (only remaining lifetime permits `null`), or rebased local timestamps overflow. Getter failures retain their cause.
invalidOption: `INVALID_OPTION`: an option such as `ttl`, `retry` or `retryDelay` is invalid; fix the options.
fetchFailed: `FETCH_FAILED`: final unclassified fetch failure after retries. Native errors keep identity when writable; immutable errors and primitive values stay reachable through `cause`. Existing foreign source/code is preserved.
setupInvalid: `RESOURCE_SETUP_INVALID`: `createResource()` got a non-function setup, or setup returned a non-function; registered cleanups already ran. Return a fetcher from setup.
setupClosed: `RESOURCE_SETUP_CLOSED`: `onDispose()` was called after setup returned, for example from an async callback; register cleanups synchronously during setup.
suspenseProbeFailed: `SUSPENSE_PROBE_FAILED`: a value thrown by the fetcher has a throwing `then` getter; both errors are kept in `errors`.

blocks.code: import { RESOURCE_SOURCE, ResourceErrorCode, type IResourceErrorCode } from '@migaia/resource'

blocks.text: 稳定错误码表，9 个码，唯一声明处 `src/error-code.ts`，包自身错误的 `source` 为 `'resource'`；已有完整外部身份的错误保留原包身份。 `RESOURCE_SOURCE` 导出这个稳定 source，跨包分类错误时应比较它与 `ResourceErrorCode`，不要复制字符串字面量。

rows: 在已 `dispose()` 的 `Resource` 上调用任意读取/操作方法
请求停止时的原生 AbortError；Resource 主动取消时与 signal.reason 同一，lifecycle replacement reason 保留在 cause
调用方显式 `cancel()` 导致当前 pending 请求被取消，`state` 落入 `cancelled` 所携带的 `DOMException`
请求取消已完成状态收敛，但取消期间的 timer/listener cleanup 失败
读取 `promise`，或在 `pending`/`idle` 状态下调用 `read()`/`peek()` 时，没有正在进行或已缓存的 Promise 可返回
非 v2 快照、负/非有限时长（remaining 可为 null）、本地重建时间戳溢出或 getter 失败
构造/调用时传入的选项（`ttl`、`retry`、`retryDelay`、`scheduler` 等）不满足取值要求
`fetcher` 抛出用于 Suspense 的值，但探测其 `.then` 时 getter 本身抛错，无法判定是否为 thenable
重试耗尽后的未分类 fetch 失败；原生错误尽量保留身份，冻结错误/非 Error 值保留在 cause，已有外部身份不改写

blocks.text: `requestAborted`/`requestCancelled` 抛出/落入状态的值始终是原生 `DOMException`（`name === 'AbortError'`），调用方通常按 `error.name === 'AbortError'` 判定并静默处理，而不是当作真实失败；`code` 只作为附加字段挂上，不改变类型。调用方应始终以 `error.code === ResourceErrorCode.xxx` 判别，不要硬编码码值字符串。

`Resource` 自己产生的错误带 `source === RESOURCE_SOURCE`（`resource`）和 `ResourceErrorCode` 里的 `code`。已经有完整 `source`/`code` 的外部错误保持原样；没有分类的加载失败在重试结束后附加 `FETCH_FAILED`，原生错误保持原类型，不可修改的错误保留在 `cause` 链上。重试策略本身出错时附加 `INVALID_OPTION`，触发它的加载错误仍可从错误链找到。取消和释放产生的错误是原生 `DOMException`（`name === 'AbortError'`），按 `error.name` 判断即可。

import { Resource, type IResourceOptions } from '@migaia/resource'
import type { IRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'

class Resource<T> implements IObserver, IDisposable {

  markDirty(): void

}

guidance.id: 取消后显示已取消而不是错误
guidance.heading: 取消后显示已取消而不是错误

blocks.text: 用户点了“取消导出”，界面却弹出“导出失败”，因为取消和失败走进了同一个 `catch`。
手写的状态通常只有“加载中、成功、失败”三种，取消只能塞进“失败”，再靠比较错误信息字符串来区分。
`cancel()` 把还在等待的请求变成 `cancelled` 状态，`state.error` 是原生 `AbortError`。资源本身没有被释放，之后调用 `refetch()` 可以重新开始。
输出：

blocks.code:
状态：cancelled
原因：AbortError
第 2 次导出完成

blocks.text: 取消后状态是 `cancelled`，原因是 `AbortError`；随后 `refetch()` 正常完成，输出“第 2 次导出完成”。
`cancelled` 是单独的状态，界面可以按 `ResourceStatus.cancelled` 显示“已取消”。取消后再读取 `state` 不会自动重启请求，只有显式调用 `refetch()` 才会。

symbols.purpose: The pure Contract package owns semantic codes for field admission, handshake selection and wire-error graph validation.
symbols.core:
callbackFailed: `CALLBACK_FAILED`: a warning, scheduler or cleanup callback failed without prior semantic identity. Native mutable errors retain identity, type and stack; other values stay on cause. Safe wire summaries do not expose callback text.
invalidDescriptor: `INVALID_DESCRIPTOR`: invalid stable component identity/version; correct local configuration.
invalidEnvelope: `INVALID_ENVELOPE`: reject the invalid semantic message without executing it.
invalidStream: `INVALID_STREAM`: reject the invalid event, sequence or value budget and terminate only its stream.
invalidFrame: `INVALID_FRAME`: discard malformed physical or empty batch framing.
frameLimitExceeded: `FRAME_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`: complete physical or retained reassembly bytes exceeded a bound.
frameAssemblyExpired: `FRAME_ASSEMBLY_EXPIRED`: not all ordered fragments arrived before the assembly timer.
invalidWireError: `INVALID_WIRE_ERROR`: reject the malformed bounded serialized error tree.
handshakeInvalid: `HANDSHAKE_INVALID`: malformed encoding, JSON or first-channel negotiation fields.
handshakeIncompatible: `HANDSHAKE_INCOMPATIBLE`: peer protocol, version or mandatory runtime baseline is incompatible.
handshakeRejected: `HANDSHAKE_REJECTED`: the remote rejected negotiation; inspect the retained remote cause.
extensionNegotiationFailed: A required extension is unavailable or received extension traffic was not negotiated. R6 / BC2 rejects it before application execution; configure compatible extensions.

symbols.name: RpcCoreErrorCode
symbols.purpose: Stable semantic failure codes owned by the runtime-neutral Core execution layer.
symbols.core:
hostTransportMissing: Exactly one genuine transport is required before opening.
hostNamespaceDuplicate: R3 / BC1 rejects duplicate transport namespaces before acquisition; choose distinct names.
featureCombinationConflict: R8 / A8 rejects two same-kind call features on one plugin; keep one complete instance.
hostPluginInvalid: A copied or fabricated object lacks registered SDK identity.
hostPeerNameDuplicate: A same-name peer is responsive, or its one probe is already pending; reject the newcomer.
callbackFailed: CALLBACK_FAILED: a construction or diagnostic callback failed; native mutable errors retain type, stack and identity, foreign semantic identities stay unchanged, and other values remain on cause.
providerGenerationMismatch: PROVIDER_GENERATION_MISMATCH: accepted caller/provider generation no longer matches the task; select the actual binding again.
forwardLoop: FORWARD_LOOP: signed route revisits this or the selected next Host; choose another route.
forwardHopLimit: FORWARD_HOP_LIMIT: three forwarding nodes were already visited; use a direct channel or shorter route.
capabilityUnsupported: CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED: actual peer agreement does not support the requested runtime mode or capability.
invalidConfig: INVALID_CONFIG: factory, component, transport or transform configuration is invalid; inspect detail and correct local inputs.
probeFailed: PROBE_FAILED: a diagnostic emit/describe/redact callback failed; business execution remains isolated.
providerDuplicated: PROVIDER_DUPLICATED: provide registered a method that already has an owner; change the method or combine providers.
protocolInvalid: PROTOCOL_INVALID: codec/protocol/envelope behavior or correlated control is invalid; inspect original cause.
contractInvalid: CONTRACT_INVALID: method correlation, direction or contract identity fields violate the actual request contract.
payloadInvalid: PAYLOAD_INVALID: data, physical batch encoding or error projection violates its selected codec boundary.
providerNotFound: PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND: the receiving endpoint has no registered provider for the requested method.
internal: INTERNAL: provider threw unexpectedly; original error stays in local diagnostics while the peer receives a redacted failure.
targetUnknown: TARGET_UNKNOWN: target or receiver is unresolved, inactive or outside the original selected binding.
endpointDisposed: ENDPOINT_DISPOSED: an operation used a disposed endpoint; construct a new owner instead.
cancelled: CANCELLED: actual caller AbortSignal cancelled the local send; remote effects may already have occurred.
deadlineExceeded: DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: the local operation deadline expired; treat this transmission attempt as failed.
contextExpired: PROVIDER_CONTEXT_EXPIRED: success or failed was called after the original provider lifetime ended; no wire effect is produced.
transport: TRANSPORT: actual physical send or terminal channel failed; preserve original transport evidence before choosing recovery. The code alone never proves nonexecution; retry requires independent evidence or idempotency/outcome reconciliation.
authenticationFailed: AUTHENTICATION_FAILED: signing, verification, encryption, decryption or original replay binding failed; details stay local.
schemaInvalid: SCHEMA_INVALID: params/result parse rejected the method data; inspect normalized issues and original cause.
capabilityConflict: CAPABILITY_CONFLICT: selected middleware/features publish conflicting keys or an ambiguous runtime instance.
overloaded: OVERLOADED: execution/replay/discovery/chunk capacity refused new work; inspect its independent reason channel.
streamResultUnknown: STREAM_RESULT_UNKNOWN: transport may have sent a stream frame before rejecting; open a new stream without replaying items.
chunkInvalid: CHUNK_INVALID: physical fragment grammar is invalid; hooks observe it and the frame is not replayed.
propertyReadFailed: PROPERTY_READ_FAILED: a getter/proxy failed without a valid synchronous reporter, or that reporter threw.
idempotencyResultUnavailable: IDEMPOTENCY_RESULT_UNAVAILABLE: business already ran but result was not retained; resolve outcome before another attempt.
stringConversionFailed: STRING_CONVERSION_FAILED: conversion or its required synchronous reporter failed; preserve original cause.

members.name: hostTransportMissing
members.description: Host creation requires one registered transport plugin. Add a transport before retrying.

members.name: hostNamespaceDuplicate
members.description: Duplicate transport namespaces are rejected before acquisition; choose distinct names.

members.name: featureCombinationConflict
members.description: Two same-kind call features on one plugin are rejected; keep one complete instance.

members.name: hostPluginInvalid
members.description: Host creation received an object without SDK registration identity. Use the define tools.

members.name: hostPeerNameDuplicate
members.description: An incoming peer name is held by a responsive session, or another admission is probing it. * Choose a different name or close the current session.

members.name: callbackFailed
members.description: A cold Probe listener, middleware installation callback, or diagnostic reporter throws. The * original remains reachable; callers repair the callback rather than retrying side effects.

members.name: providerGenerationMismatch
members.description: The selected authenticated provider/caller generation no longer matches this task; select * again.

members.name: forwardLoop
members.description: A signed route already contains this Host or the selected next Host. Forwarding rejects before * admission and sending; callers must choose a route that does not revisit a Host.

members.name: forwardHopLimit
members.description: Three forwarding nodes have already been visited. Forwarding rejects a fourth before admission * and sending; callers may establish a direct connect/listen channel instead.

members.name: capabilityUnsupported
members.description: A Runtime API operation requires a mode or capability absent from the actual peer agreement. * Choose a supported method/mode rather than retrying the same operation.

members.name: invalidConfig
members.description: A factory, middleware, or transport descriptor or configuration field is invalid. Replay * protection also rejects encrypt-only configuration, unavailable entropy, and exhausted * counters. * * This code identifies argument and configuration failures. The caller corrects the configuration * using `detail` before retrying.

members.name: probeFailed
members.description: A probe emit, describe or redact callback, or a native observation disposer, fails. The * installed probe retains the original cause and isolates diagnostic failure from business * execution; callers should repair or disable the diagnostic sink or its cleanup callback.

members.name: providerDuplicated
members.description: `provide()` registers the same method twice. * * A provider does not replace another provider with the same name. The caller combines the * implementations or changes the name.

members.name: protocolInvalid
members.description: A protocol codec, scheme, or envelope is invalid, the caller cannot reconstruct a response * error, or a provider receives an invalid abort payload. This is the base code for * `RpcProtocolError`. * * The caller checks that the protocol configuration matches the peer scheme. If the payload is * already sent or cancellation has taken effect, inspect the peer rather than retrying the same * message.

members.name: contractInvalid
members.description: Contract fields, direction, or request/response correlation are invalid. This is the base code * for `RpcContractError`. * * The caller checks `version`, `identifier`, sender/target direction, or `taskId`/method * correlation.

members.name: payloadInvalid
members.description: A codec payload violates its input rules, or sender-side error serialization degrades a read or * data projection. This is the base code for `RpcSerializationError`. Physical batch * shape/encoding failures preserve the contract cause; malformed semantic members are reported * individually without discarding valid siblings. * * The caller checks the data, codec, or thrown value. Do not retry the same payload if it is * already sent or cancellation has taken effect.

members.name: providerNotFound
members.description: The provider executor cannot find a provider for the target method (`Provider not found`). * * The caller checks whether `provide()` registers the method. Do not retry the failed lookup. * This is the wire code for an inbound provider lookup failure.

members.name: internal
members.description: A provider throws an unhandled exception. This is the standard code for an `INTERNAL` response. * * Only local hooks receive the redacted original exception. The peer receives `RpcRemoteError` * with code `INTERNAL`.

members.name: targetUnknown
members.description: A target or receiver is unresolved, inactive, or outside the current binding. * * The caller checks whether `targetId` is registered or discovered, or whether `receiverSelector` * returns an unknown receiver.

members.name: endpointDisposed
members.description: An endpoint operation runs after disposal (`RpcLifecycleError`). * * The caller creates a new endpoint instead of reusing the closed instance.

members.name: keepaliveQuotaExceeded
members.description: A keepalive call admitted during Session closing exceeds its in-flight prepared-message quota. * Captured metadata, manifests and native sidecars count before optional feature overhead. The * caller reduces the payload or waits for existing work to settle; final close is uncharged.

members.name: cancelled
members.description: The caller's `AbortSignal` cancels a local send (`RpcAbortError`). * * The caller handles this cooperative cancellation separately from remote failures.

members.name: deadlineExceeded
members.description: A local deadline expires (`RpcTimeoutError`). * * The caller checks target reachability and the timeout duration. Treat the request failure as * the result of this transmission attempt.

members.name: contextExpired
members.description: `ctx.success()` or `ctx.failed()` runs after the provider task ends. * * The expired result produces no wire effects. The caller keeps response logic within the * provider's synchronous or awaited lifetime.

members.name: transport
members.description: A transport send fails, a terminal event occurs, or the transport closes (`RpcTransportError`). * * The code alone does not establish whether a send already executed. Retry only with independent * evidence that it did not execute, or use the existing idempotency/outcome reconciliation.

members.name: authenticationFailed
members.description: A per-frame authentication transform fails during encryption, signing, verification, or * decryption (`RpcAuthenticationError`). Replay protection rejects missing/invalid binding, * duplicate counters and untrusted physical sessions. * * The caller checks key and algorithm configuration. Failure details are not sent back to the * peer.

members.name: schemaInvalid
members.description: Method parameters or results violate the contract schema (`RpcSchemaValidationError`). * * The caller corrects the data using `data.issues` rather than retrying the same invalid data.

members.name: capabilityConflict
members.description: A capability is published twice, or a frozen capability registry receives another write. Also * rejects folded Feature method collisions and ambiguous runtime instances. * * The caller checks middleware for duplicate declarations of reserved capabilities. This is a * configuration error.

members.name: overloaded
members.description: A local capacity limit rejects new work in provider admission, the replay ledger, discovery * waiters, outbound IDs, or chunks. * * The caller reduces concurrency, shortens TTL, or increases capacity. This signals backpressure * rather than a logic error.

members.name: streamResultUnknown
members.description: A stream frame may have been sent before its transport rejected; the caller must open a fresh * stream and never replay delivered values.

members.name: chunkInvalid
members.description: A chunk frame has an invalid format. This is the base code for `RpcChunkError`. * * The caller checks chunk configuration (`chunkSize` ≥ 4) and the peer implementation. An invalid * frame only invokes hooks and is not retried.

members.name: propertyReadFailed
members.description: A getter or Proxy throws during `safeRead` without a synchronous reporter, or the reporter * itself throws. The caller repairs the input or supplies a synchronous `report` at a boundary * that owns a diagnostic sink.

members.name: idempotencyResultUnavailable
members.description: A keyed call already executed but its result was not retained for replay. The caller must * resolve the outcome before issuing another non-idempotent attempt.

members.name: stringConversionFailed
members.description: A string conversion throws without a synchronous reporter, or its reporter throws (cleanup ). * The caller must repair the input or provide a synchronous diagnostic sink.

hostTransportMissing: Exactly one genuine transport is required before opening.
hostNamespaceDuplicate: R3 / BC1 rejects duplicate transport namespaces before acquisition; choose distinct names.
featureCombinationConflict: R8 / A8 rejects two same-kind call features on one plugin; keep one complete instance.
hostPluginInvalid: A copied or fabricated object lacks registered SDK identity.
hostPeerNameDuplicate: A same-name peer is responsive, or its one probe is already pending; reject the newcomer.
callbackFailed: CALLBACK_FAILED: a construction or diagnostic callback failed; native mutable errors retain type, stack and identity, foreign semantic identities stay unchanged, and other values remain on cause.
providerGenerationMismatch: PROVIDER_GENERATION_MISMATCH: accepted caller/provider generation no longer matches the task; select the actual binding again.
forwardLoop: FORWARD_LOOP: signed route revisits this or the selected next Host; choose another route.
forwardHopLimit: FORWARD_HOP_LIMIT: three forwarding nodes were already visited; use a direct channel or shorter route.
capabilityUnsupported: CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED: actual peer agreement does not support the requested runtime mode or capability.
invalidConfig: INVALID_CONFIG: factory, component, transport or transform configuration is invalid; inspect detail and correct local inputs.
probeFailed: PROBE_FAILED: a diagnostic emit/describe/redact callback failed; business execution remains isolated.
providerDuplicated: PROVIDER_DUPLICATED: provide registered a method that already has an owner; change the method or combine providers.
protocolInvalid: PROTOCOL_INVALID: codec/protocol/envelope behavior or correlated control is invalid; inspect original cause.
contractInvalid: CONTRACT_INVALID: method correlation, direction or contract identity fields violate the actual request contract.
payloadInvalid: PAYLOAD_INVALID: data, physical batch encoding or error projection violates its selected codec boundary.
providerNotFound: PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND: the receiving endpoint has no registered provider for the requested method.
internal: INTERNAL: provider threw unexpectedly; original error stays in local diagnostics while the peer receives a redacted failure.
targetUnknown: TARGET_UNKNOWN: target or receiver is unresolved, inactive or outside the original selected binding.
endpointDisposed: ENDPOINT_DISPOSED: an operation used a disposed endpoint; construct a new owner instead.
cancelled: CANCELLED: actual caller AbortSignal cancelled the local send; remote effects may already have occurred.
deadlineExceeded: DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: the local operation deadline expired; treat this transmission attempt as failed.
contextExpired: PROVIDER_CONTEXT_EXPIRED: success or failed was called after the original provider lifetime ended; no wire effect is produced.
transport: TRANSPORT: actual physical send or terminal channel failed; preserve original transport evidence before choosing recovery. The code alone never proves nonexecution; retry requires independent evidence or idempotency/outcome reconciliation.
authenticationFailed: AUTHENTICATION_FAILED: signing, verification, encryption, decryption or original replay binding failed; details stay local.
schemaInvalid: SCHEMA_INVALID: params/result parse rejected the method data; inspect normalized issues and original cause.
capabilityConflict: CAPABILITY_CONFLICT: selected middleware/features publish conflicting keys or an ambiguous runtime instance.
overloaded: OVERLOADED: execution/replay/discovery/chunk capacity refused new work; inspect its independent reason channel.
streamResultUnknown: STREAM_RESULT_UNKNOWN: transport may have sent a stream frame before rejecting; open a new stream without replaying items.
chunkInvalid: CHUNK_INVALID: physical fragment grammar is invalid; hooks observe it and the frame is not replayed.
propertyReadFailed: PROPERTY_READ_FAILED: a getter/proxy failed without a valid synchronous reporter, or that reporter threw.
idempotencyResultUnavailable: IDEMPOTENCY_RESULT_UNAVAILABLE: business already ran but result was not retained; resolve outcome before another attempt.
stringConversionFailed: STRING_CONVERSION_FAILED: conversion or its required synchronous reporter failed; preserve original cause.

blocks.text: 线上错误为`{root,nodes}`。每个节点必须有source/code/name/message/stack，cause为节点索引，errors为有序索引数组，可带data/route/truncated。共享与循环边通过索引表达；接收端须检查索引、节点和累计预算。
节点上限为 1024；包含 1025 个节点的输入以原 `TypeError` / `INVALID_WIRE_ERROR` 拒绝。旧错误树的 64 层深度规则不适用于 flat 图的边。还原先为每个节点创建一个错误对象，再迭代接上引用，因此一个节点被多次引用时保持 `===`，环也指回同一批已还原对象；这不表示跨进程对象与发送端保持 `===`。
跨realm恢复会创建新错误对象，不能保留跨进程的`===`；支持的原生类与发送方stack保持。`serializeRpcWireError`要求report，读取/投影失败保留在本地报告；超预算裁剪会标truncated，不承诺每次文本裁剪都触发report。
独立错误树工具`serializeRpcError/deserializeRpcError/normalizeRpcSerializedError/reachRpcError`仍在`/errors`，用于纯诊断边界。wire业务协议只用flat图。恢复后的source/code是诊断，不授予本地控制权限；不能据对端填写的code决定本地资源所有权。

blocks.text: 线上错误为`{root,nodes}`。每个节点必须有source/code/name/message/stack，cause为节点索引，errors为有序索引数组，可带data/route/truncated。共享与循环边通过索引表达；接收端须检查索引、节点和累计预算。
节点上限为 1024；包含 1025 个节点的输入以原 `TypeError` / `INVALID_WIRE_ERROR` 拒绝。旧错误树的 64 层深度规则不适用于 flat 图的边。还原先为每个节点创建一个错误对象，再迭代接上引用，因此一个节点被多次引用时保持 `===`，环也指回同一批已还原对象；这不表示跨进程对象与发送端保持 `===`。
跨realm恢复会创建新错误对象，不能保留跨进程的`===`；支持的原生类与发送方stack保持。`serializeRpcWireError`要求report，读取/投影失败保留在本地报告；超预算裁剪会标truncated，不承诺每次文本裁剪都触发report。
独立错误树工具`serializeRpcError/deserializeRpcError/normalizeRpcSerializedError/reachRpcError`仍在`/errors`，用于纯诊断边界。wire业务协议只用flat图。恢复后的source/code是诊断，不授予本地控制权限；不能据对端填写的code决定本地资源所有权。

Import the canonical field instead of duplicating its wording.

blocks.text: 线上错误为`{root,nodes}`。每个节点必须有source/code/name/message/stack，cause为节点索引，errors为有序索引数组，可带data/route/truncated。共享与循环边通过索引表达；接收端须检查索引、节点和累计预算。
节点上限为 1024；包含 1025 个节点的输入以原 `TypeError` / `INVALID_WIRE_ERROR` 拒绝。旧错误树的 64 层深度规则不适用于 flat 图的边。还原先为每个节点创建一个错误对象，再迭代接上引用，因此一个节点被多次引用时保持 `===`，环也指回同一批已还原对象；这不表示跨进程对象与发送端保持 `===`。
跨realm恢复会创建新错误对象，不能保留跨进程的`===`；支持的原生类与发送方stack保持。`serializeRpcWireError`要求report，读取/投影失败保留在本地报告；超预算裁剪会标truncated，不承诺每次文本裁剪都触发report。
独立错误树工具`serializeRpcError/deserializeRpcError/normalizeRpcSerializedError/reachRpcError`仍在`/errors`，用于纯诊断边界。wire业务协议只用flat图。恢复后的source/code是诊断，不授予本地控制权限；不能据对端填写的code决定本地资源所有权。

symbols.purpose: Projects any original thrown value into a bounded wire error tree while preserving semantic source/code, native name, remote stack and cause/aggregate descendants. Omitted unreadable data is reported. This standalone tree boundary is distinct from the protocol flat graph.

blocks.text: 线上错误为`{root,nodes}`。每个节点必须有source/code/name/message/stack，cause为节点索引，errors为有序索引数组，可带data/route/truncated。共享与循环边通过索引表达；接收端须检查索引、节点和累计预算。
节点上限为 1024；包含 1025 个节点的输入以原 `TypeError` / `INVALID_WIRE_ERROR` 拒绝。旧错误树的 64 层深度规则不适用于 flat 图的边。还原先为每个节点创建一个错误对象，再迭代接上引用，因此一个节点被多次引用时保持 `===`，环也指回同一批已还原对象；这不表示跨进程对象与发送端保持 `===`。
跨realm恢复会创建新错误对象，不能保留跨进程的`===`；支持的原生类与发送方stack保持。`serializeRpcWireError`要求report，读取/投影失败保留在本地报告；超预算裁剪会标truncated，不承诺每次文本裁剪都触发report。
独立错误树工具`serializeRpcError/deserializeRpcError/normalizeRpcSerializedError/reachRpcError`仍在`/errors`，用于纯诊断边界。wire业务协议只用flat图。恢复后的source/code是诊断，不授予本地控制权限；不能据对端填写的code决定本地资源所有权。

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
observation: Optional actual native observation port; absence must not be advertised as carrier-stage capability.
No native observation subscription.
id: Correlation id issued by the originating call or control owner and echoed by its terminal.
nativeBinary: True only for a carrier with genuine native backing support; caller metadata cannot enable it.
codecs: Ordered real codec proposals including mandatory json bootstrap.
codec: Actual executing codec for this physical carrier.
assertTransfer: Reject explicit transfer when this acquired medium cannot perform it.
Normal return proves support, without creating caller permission.
subscribe: Install the Host receiver on this actual connection.
subscribe.receiver: Host-owned frame/close/error callbacks for this binding.
Exact native listener cleanup owned by this installation.
write: Hand one opaque codec frame to the real ordered physical writer.
write.frame: Frame from the same carrier codec or a negotiated frame plugin.
write.options: Optional local signal, transfer, lane, trace and handoff notification.
Completes at physical acceptance, not queue insertion; failures retain their original diagnostic.
close: Close the actual resource and borrow its original idempotent completion.
close.reason: Original local reason from the closing or departing owner.
The resource-owned close Promise; cleanup failures retain their original cause/errors chain.

symbols.name: normalizePortable
symbols.purpose:
Snapshots supported portable values without sending or executing a request. The default wire domain is null, boolean, finite number, string, array, plain record or a canonical bytes tag; Uint8Array becomes {$rpc: "bytes", base64url}. Records become frozen null-prototype snapshots.

Rejects cycles, nonfinite numbers and unsupported objects with INVALID_ENVELOPE. Ordinary record getters are read once and can execute user code. Native binary belongs to an independently negotiated profile, not the default wire result.
symbols.core:
value: Application or peer value requiring a portable data-only snapshot.
depth: Optional existing traversal depth, default 0 at the root; RPC_PORTABLE_MAX_DEPTH is 64. Ordinary application calls omit this traversal-integration parameter.
active: Optional caller-provided ancestor Set for the same traversal, default undefined with traversal-local cycle tracking. It tracks active ancestors rather than deduplicating all repeated references.
nativeBinary: Optional native-binary branch flag, default false; true admits native bytes, or a synchronous rejection callback supplies the failure boundary.
errorMetadata: Optional caller-owned summary/route map ports; omission uses no retained provenance store.
IRpcWirePortableValue by default, or negotiated IRpcPortableValue with native binary enabled; invalid data throws INVALID_ENVELOPE.
parameters: value: unknown
depth: number (optional)
active: Set<object> (optional)
nativeBinary: false (optional)
errorMetadata: IRpcErrorWireMetadata (optional)
depth: number
active: Set<object>
nativeBinary: boolean | (() => never)
symbols.returns: IRpcWirePortableValue | IRpcPortableValue
examples:
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { normalizePortable } from '@migaia/rpc-contract/portable'

const source = { profile: { name: 'Ada' }, bytes: new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3]) }
const snapshot = normalizePortable(source)
source.profile.name = 'Grace'
source.bytes[0] = 99
assert.equal(
  JSON.stringify(snapshot),
  '{"profile":{"name":"Ada"},"bytes":{"$rpc":"bytes","base64url":"AQID"}}'
)
assert.equal(Object.isFrozen(snapshot), true)
console.log('portable snapshot preserved')

blocks.text: 线上错误为`{root,nodes}`。每个节点必须有source/code/name/message/stack，cause为节点索引，errors为有序索引数组，可带data/route/truncated。共享与循环边通过索引表达；接收端须检查索引、节点和累计预算。
节点上限为 1024；包含 1025 个节点的输入以原 `TypeError` / `INVALID_WIRE_ERROR` 拒绝。旧错误树的 64 层深度规则不适用于 flat 图的边。还原先为每个节点创建一个错误对象，再迭代接上引用，因此一个节点被多次引用时保持 `===`，环也指回同一批已还原对象；这不表示跨进程对象与发送端保持 `===`。
跨realm恢复会创建新错误对象，不能保留跨进程的`===`；支持的原生类与发送方stack保持。`serializeRpcWireError`要求report，读取/投影失败保留在本地报告；超预算裁剪会标truncated，不承诺每次文本裁剪都触发report。
独立错误树工具`serializeRpcError/deserializeRpcError/normalizeRpcSerializedError/reachRpcError`仍在`/errors`，用于纯诊断边界。wire业务协议只用flat图。恢复后的source/code是诊断，不授予本地控制权限；不能据对端填写的code决定本地资源所有权。

symbols.core:
open: Producer opens an admitted stream at sequence zero.
pull: Consumer grants credit for exactly one next item.
item: Producer sends the one item authorized by held credit.
end: Producer reports normal completion of the stream.
fail: Producer reports a serialized terminal failure.
cancel: Retained stream vocabulary; the sole semantic grammar cancels through its correlated cancel envelope, not an extra stream event shape.
cancelled: Producer acknowledges actual stream cancellation.

symbols.name: RpcWireField
symbols.purpose: Closed-shape field names are vocabulary; a listed key is not valid on every frame.
symbols.core:
generation: Actual Session or restart generation; copied wire diagnostics cannot create native ownership.
extension: Selects the outer negotiated extension identity.
profile: Fixed `migaia.rpc/2` semantic profile; the sender selects no legacy fallback.
kind: Closed frame discriminator selecting which remaining fields are admitted.
id: Correlation id issued by the originating call or control owner and echoed by its terminal.
route: Routing facts supplied by the actual sending owner; forwarding preserves the selected task.
task: Original caller, method and selected generation tuple; terminal frames must echo it.
options: Closed wire options for ordering, cancellation scope and idempotency; no local signal or feature instance.
payload: Optional admitted portable business input; actual undefined is represented by omission.
reason: Optional original terminal reason, represented as a flat error graph on the wire.
stream: Selects the stream slot in the wire shape and its diagnostic pointer.
completion: Actual business terminal including stream cleanup; it is not merely physical write completion.
idempotencyKey: Origin-issued bounded operation token reused only for the same semantic operation.
outcome: Selects the outcome slot in the wire shape and its diagnostic pointer.
callerId: Original caller instance id captured at call creation, not the current intermediary.
callerGeneration: Original caller generation issued by the actual Session or restart owner.
targetGeneration: Exact destination generation chosen for this operation; replacement cannot settle the old operation.
method: Declared method name from the accepted provider directory; not an arbitrary Host property path.
providerId: Provider instance address issued with the corresponding generation fact.
orderKey: Caller-selected FIFO key within the real provider owner; no physical queue is created by the type.
cancel: Only `before-start` limits cancellation to work not yet admitted to business execution.
result: Admitted portable business result; an actual undefined result is omitted.
error: Original local failure or admitted flat error graph, as selected by the surrounding contract.
event: Selects the event slot in the wire shape and its diagnostic pointer.
source: Stable diagnostic source supplied by the originating error owner; not authentication authority.
code: Semantic diagnostic code retained independently of presentation text; remote codes grant no local control.
name: Owner-issued name used for the surrounding identity or diagnostic shape.
message: Bounded error presentation text; do not parse it to authorize retries or resource retirement.
stack: Original sender stack string; restoration does not substitute a receiving-side stack.
data: Portable diagnostic detail or carrier-owned opaque data, as specified by the enclosing type.
truncated: Present only as true when the bounded projection omits graph or text content.
applicationVersion: Application-defined nonempty version label for this route, separate from protocol 2.0.
senderId: Immediate sending instance address supplied by the accepted source owner.
receiverId: Selected immediate receiving instance address; intermediaries cannot infer it from a payload.
targetId: Original logical target address selected by the caller; forwarding retains this destination.
sentAt: Sender-supplied nonnegative timestamp; it does not replace the local monotonic deadline clock.
forwardRoute: Bounded ordered Host node ids already traversed; diagnostic data grants no forwarding permission.
trace: Explicit caller correlation containing 1–256 printable ASCII characters; only this operation and its transparent forwarding inherit it.
remainingMs: Remaining relative deadline budget from the previous owner; forwarding can only reduce it.
major: Selects the major slot in the wire shape and its diagnostic pointer.
minor: Selects the minor slot in the wire shape and its diagnostic pointer.
codec: Actual codec selected from the bilateral handshake proposals.
extensions: Actual extension proposals, selected membership or per-operation data, according to the enclosing contract.
self: Current genuine local identity supplied by the Host or verified native bootstrap owner.
methods: Actual compiled method descriptions belonging to this provider or accepted Session.
nodeId: Optional accepted Host node id used for loop diagnostics, not a native process identity.
sidecars: Ordered original complete backing identities supplied by the same codec; not copied protocol data.
auth: Optional portable data supplied by the actual auth owner; pure negotiation does not verify credentials.
steps: Ordered request-only group steps; not physical batching.
operation: The selected outcome lookup/result or control ping/pong/drain operation in its closed record.
state: Group success/failure/not-executed or outcome pending/unknown/done, according to its enclosing record.
store: Actual store kind, epoch and continuity accompanying this lookup.
mode: request, notify, stream, group or outcome selects this operation grammar.
value: Mode-dependent portable value or generation ordinal in its own closed record.
timeoutMs: Retained scalar vocabulary; not an allowed local timeout instance or numeric option on wire call options.
ok: True selects an optional result; false requires the flat error graph.
seq: Nonnegative safe integer issued by the corresponding stream participant.
epoch: Opaque epoch issued by the actual available store, not a caller-generated generation.
continuity: retained, lost-since-restart or unavailable describes actual store custody.
root: Valid zero-based selected root index, not necessarily zero.
nodes: Bounded error nodes whose cause/errors indices must all reference this array.
cause: Optional zero-based index into this graph nodes array.
errors: Nonempty ordered aggregate child indices into the same nodes array.
step: Exactly hello; all versions/codecs/extensions are proposals, not selected authority.
versions: Unique offered major/minor revisions; this implementation speaks 2.0.
codecs: Ordered unique actual codec ids, including the mandatory json baseline.
requiredExtensions: Optional subset whose absence must reject negotiation.
peer: Original diagnostic peer identity; not an authenticated principal.
runtime: Bounded lowercase runtime label such as node, python or a valid custom label.
runtimeVersion: Optional display version; absence is preserved.
implementation: Optional implementation name/version display record; not an extension declaration.
directory: Original local schemaVersion 3 identity and methods.

instanceId: Actual Host instance id issued by its identity owner, distinct from display name.
supportedModes: Nonempty unique request/notify/stream modes actually offered by this route.
modeSource: declared records explicit contract metadata; generated-routes records compiled routes.
idempotent: Optional request replay declaration; not proof that an optional replay implementation is installed.
forwardedVia: Optional immediate forwarding connection name supplied by the directory owner.
input: Optional admitted input schema; actual validation belongs to the schema plugin.
output: Optional admitted result schema; no validation runs during directory inspection.
yield: Optional admitted stream element schema.
manifest: Optional protected binary manifest from this same preparation.
storage: inline or native selected by the real carrier; payload flags cannot grant support.
envelope: The original admitted operational envelope associated with these native leaves.
backings: Ordered complete backing descriptors, each with byteLength and SHA-256 text.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Closed-shape field names are vocabulary; a listed key is not valid on every frame.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import RpcWireField from @migaia/rpc-contract/protocol, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use RpcWireField when its const contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when RpcWireField does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained const example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法

blocks.text: 线上错误为`{root,nodes}`。每个节点必须有source/code/name/message/stack，cause为节点索引，errors为有序索引数组，可带data/route/truncated。共享与循环边通过索引表达；接收端须检查索引、节点和累计预算。
节点上限为 1024；包含 1025 个节点的输入以原 `TypeError` / `INVALID_WIRE_ERROR` 拒绝。旧错误树的 64 层深度规则不适用于 flat 图的边。还原先为每个节点创建一个错误对象，再迭代接上引用，因此一个节点被多次引用时保持 `===`，环也指回同一批已还原对象；这不表示跨进程对象与发送端保持 `===`。
跨realm恢复会创建新错误对象，不能保留跨进程的`===`；支持的原生类与发送方stack保持。`serializeRpcWireError`要求report，读取/投影失败保留在本地报告；超预算裁剪会标truncated，不承诺每次文本裁剪都触发report。
独立错误树工具`serializeRpcError/deserializeRpcError/normalizeRpcSerializedError/reachRpcError`仍在`/errors`，用于纯诊断边界。wire业务协议只用flat图。恢复后的source/code是诊断，不授予本地控制权限；不能据对端填写的code决定本地资源所有权。

blocks.text: verifier 或凭据解析器抛出、拒绝时，auth 在本地错误的 `cause` 上保留原始错误。用 `errorMapFeature(map)` 决定对端能看到哪些错误信息，例如把含凭据的细节换成公开提示。本地抛出的错误、`report`、警告和只读观察插件看到的仍是原始错误，与插件安装先后无关。它可放在宿主 `plugins` 或传输 `features`，传输级覆盖宿主级。

`map(error, context)` 必须同步返回 `Error`、可移植值或 `undefined`。返回值就是发给对端的错误内容，不自动附加原错的原因链。回调抛错或返回值无法序列化时，报告映射失败，并按未映射时的规则发送原错误。返回 Promise/thenable 时报告 `INVALID_CONFIG`，立即按原规则发送，不等待它，因此同一会话的后续消息不会被它卡住；迟到的 Promise 拒绝仍会单独报告。
没有 `errorMapFeature` 时，未认证对端收到的握手拒绝默认隐藏细节；其他错误保留完整的原因链。跨进程或线程会还原成新对象，不保证与发送方原错 `===`。需要隐藏对端可见信息时配置映射，本地日志和原因链仍可用于排查。
连接或 Auth 安装在验签中途关闭时，这次入站处理按取消结束，不再报告为认证失败；原始取消原因仍保留，真正的验签失败照常报告。直接执行 Auth SDK 阶段的调用者，在安装关闭后会得到现有的 `UtilsAbortError` 及原始 `cause`，而不是 `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`。

symbols.name: IRpcNotifyOptions
symbols.signature:
export type IRpcNotifyOptions<Support extends boolean = false> =
  IRpcCallOptions<Support> & Readonly<{ targetId?: string }>;
symbols.purpose: Call options with a direct target override for one-way delivery; physical completion is not a business acknowledgement.
symbols.core:
timeout: Complete timeout feature or false for this invocation; an inherited chain deadline still bounds the attempt.
Inherit the transport feature, then link policy.
retry: Complete originating retry feature or false; transit forwarding never executes this strategy.
signal: Caller signal observed before admission and throughout completion. Cancelling a provider does not roll back side effects or kill a native process.
No caller signal.
transfer: Original ArrayBuffer list for native media supporting transfer. Unsupported media reject synchronously without reading a caller transfer getter.
No transfer requested.
trace: Application diagnostic correlation text propagated within protocol bounds, without granting authority.
No explicit trace.
idempotencyKey: Stable logical key issued by the originating application or retry keyFactory. A key alone does not install server-side deduplication.
No explicit logical key.
targetId: Accepted direct peer name or instance identity in this namespace, obtained from actual peer/member identity.
Select all current direct targets.
orderKey: Application ordering key; the shared provider FIFO starts same-key work in acceptance order and releases its receipt on every terminal path.
No ordering-key lane.
cancel: Explicit before-start cancellation policy for queued provider work; it does not roll back work that already entered the provider.
Canonical call cancellation behavior.
Cancel while provider work is still queued before entry.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
