blocks.text: IStoreReadyBarrier 工厂为 `()=>Promise<unknown> 或 unknown`，归一化会同步调用它，结果用 Promise.resolve 接纳。所有屏障成功后渲染子树，任一失败在 render 抛给外层 Error Boundary；Provider 自己不提供错误 UI。Error 原因保持原实例（包括冻结 Error），非 Error 原因以 READY_REJECTED 包装并在 cause 保留，不进行字符串强制转换。features.wasm 的屏障可为任何等价初始化，不强制使用 store-wasm；ensureWasm 是可选组合。

同一 Provider/barrierScope、同一 ready 数组身份复用列表 Promise；新数组产生新就绪代，即使元素相同也重建 ReadyBoundary，旧代完成不能放行新代。工厂结果另按 scope+factory 身份缓存，在途/成功结果可跨列表复用，失败后删除工厂缓存，但同一旧数组仍复用已缓存的失败列表 Promise；单换数组不保证重新运行已成功的工厂。不同 Provider/请求 scope 隔离。abandoned render 之间不保证工厂恰好运行一次；非幂等初始化应由应用 owner 提供稳定 Promise。

已完成 Promise 的状态仍在 then 微任务更新，因此首次同步渲染可能 pending；客户端 effect 会重查，SSR renderToString 不运行 effect。保持 ready 数组、Store/Signal/Resource、selector/equality 身份稳定；配置是 readonly 输入，改变配置时提供新对象，不在 render 中写状态或创建持有资源的业务实例。

归一化配置的 features.wasm 为 boolean，features.experimental 为空原型浅冻结白名单，defaults 含 warnAsyncActions，ready 为 null 或带 promise/status()/error() 的跟踪对象；状态为 pending/ready/error；只有实验白名单被冻结，外层 features/defaults/ready 容器不保证冻结。StoreProviderState/IStoreProviderState 公开这三个值，状态不是错误码。实验键排序编码使输入键次序不影响配置；访问器不作为开启数据且不执行 getter，`__proto__` 是普通键。

blocks.text: IStoreReadyBarrier 工厂为 `()=>Promise<unknown> 或 unknown`，归一化会同步调用它，结果用 Promise.resolve 接纳。所有屏障成功后渲染子树，任一失败在 render 抛给外层 Error Boundary；Provider 自己不提供错误 UI。Error 原因保持原实例（包括冻结 Error），非 Error 原因以 READY_REJECTED 包装并在 cause 保留，不进行字符串强制转换。features.wasm 的屏障可为任何等价初始化，不强制使用 store-wasm；ensureWasm 是可选组合。

同一 Provider/barrierScope、同一 ready 数组身份复用列表 Promise；新数组产生新就绪代，即使元素相同也重建 ReadyBoundary，旧代完成不能放行新代。工厂结果另按 scope+factory 身份缓存，在途/成功结果可跨列表复用，失败后删除工厂缓存，但同一旧数组仍复用已缓存的失败列表 Promise；单换数组不保证重新运行已成功的工厂。不同 Provider/请求 scope 隔离。abandoned render 之间不保证工厂恰好运行一次；非幂等初始化应由应用 owner 提供稳定 Promise。

已完成 Promise 的状态仍在 then 微任务更新，因此首次同步渲染可能 pending；客户端 effect 会重查，SSR renderToString 不运行 effect。保持 ready 数组、Store/Signal/Resource、selector/equality 身份稳定；配置是 readonly 输入，改变配置时提供新对象，不在 render 中写状态或创建持有资源的业务实例。

归一化配置的 features.wasm 为 boolean，features.experimental 为空原型浅冻结白名单，defaults 含 warnAsyncActions，ready 为 null 或带 promise/status()/error() 的跟踪对象；状态为 pending/ready/error；只有实验白名单被冻结，外层 features/defaults/ready 容器不保证冻结。StoreProviderState/IStoreProviderState 公开这三个值，状态不是错误码。实验键排序编码使输入键次序不影响配置；访问器不作为开启数据且不执行 getter，`__proto__` 是普通键。

blocks.text: IStoreReadyBarrier 工厂为 `()=>Promise<unknown> 或 unknown`，归一化会同步调用它，结果用 Promise.resolve 接纳。所有屏障成功后渲染子树，任一失败在 render 抛给外层 Error Boundary；Provider 自己不提供错误 UI。Error 原因保持原实例（包括冻结 Error），非 Error 原因以 READY_REJECTED 包装并在 cause 保留，不进行字符串强制转换。features.wasm 的屏障可为任何等价初始化，不强制使用 store-wasm；ensureWasm 是可选组合。

同一 Provider/barrierScope、同一 ready 数组身份复用列表 Promise；新数组产生新就绪代，即使元素相同也重建 ReadyBoundary，旧代完成不能放行新代。工厂结果另按 scope+factory 身份缓存，在途/成功结果可跨列表复用，失败后删除工厂缓存，但同一旧数组仍复用已缓存的失败列表 Promise；单换数组不保证重新运行已成功的工厂。不同 Provider/请求 scope 隔离。abandoned render 之间不保证工厂恰好运行一次；非幂等初始化应由应用 owner 提供稳定 Promise。

ready: Promises or zero-argument synchronous/async factories. Rejected factory results leave the factory cache; scopes are isolated. A changed array identity selects a new Provider generation and ReadyBoundary, so an old generation cannot release the new one; changing only the array does not rerun a successful cached factory.
Factory result is awaited and discarded; rejection blocks the subtree and reaches its outer Error Boundary.

fallback: ReactNode rendered while readiness remains pending; rejected barriers throw instead of rendering this fallback.

sections.title: 高阶用法
sections.content:
Direct Store and Signal hooks retain their source Runtime. Atom protocol hooks with a definition bridge route to the Provider AtomStore; unregistering the component releases subscriptions without disposing borrowed sources.
Readiness blocks the subtree but does not initialize WASM automatically. External registries remain caller-owned unless disposeOnUnmount is true.
Provide independent atom state per subtree and gate rendering on application initialization.

blocks.text: IStoreReadyBarrier 工厂为 `()=>Promise<unknown> 或 unknown`，归一化会同步调用它，结果用 Promise.resolve 接纳。所有屏障成功后渲染子树，任一失败在 render 抛给外层 Error Boundary；Provider 自己不提供错误 UI。Error 原因保持原实例（包括冻结 Error），非 Error 原因以 READY_REJECTED 包装并在 cause 保留，不进行字符串强制转换。features.wasm 的屏障可为任何等价初始化，不强制使用 store-wasm；ensureWasm 是可选组合。

同一 Provider/barrierScope、同一 ready 数组身份复用列表 Promise；新数组产生新就绪代，即使元素相同也重建 ReadyBoundary，旧代完成不能放行新代。工厂结果另按 scope+factory 身份缓存，在途/成功结果可跨列表复用，失败后删除工厂缓存，但同一旧数组仍复用已缓存的失败列表 Promise；单换数组不保证重新运行已成功的工厂。不同 Provider/请求 scope 隔离。abandoned render 之间不保证工厂恰好运行一次；非幂等初始化应由应用 owner 提供稳定 Promise。

已完成 Promise 的状态仍在 then 微任务更新，因此首次同步渲染可能 pending；客户端 effect 会重查，SSR renderToString 不运行 effect。保持 ready 数组、Store/Signal/Resource、selector/equality 身份稳定；配置是 readonly 输入，改变配置时提供新对象，不在 render 中写状态或创建持有资源的业务实例。

symbols.purpose: Stable codes for Registry admission/disposal, Provider requirements, feature gates and readiness failures.
symbols.core:
registryDisposed: Registry lookup or mutation after its lifecycle left open.
registryDisposalFailed: Owned cleanup failed: a mutable native uncoded error keeps identity and gains this code; frozen or non-Error values remain on cause/errors. Foreign coded errors keep their owner; multiple failures form an ordered native AggregateError.
providerRequired: Provider-dependent hook or feature assertion has no Provider configuration.
featureDisabled: Feature assertion targets a flag not explicitly enabled.
storeMissing: Required token has no current Registry entry.
storeDuplicate: Register attempts to insert an already registered token.
crossRuntime: Registered reactive value belongs to another Runtime graph.
invalidConfig: Malformed token, ownership, Provider config or readiness declaration.
readyRejected: Readiness rejected with a non-Error value; wrapper retains that original value in cause.
parameters: This const declaration has no parameters.

members.name: registryDisposed
members.description: A provider registry is registered with or read after `dispose()`. * * Create a new registry instead of reusing the disposed instance.

members.name: registryDisposalFailed
members.description: An owned registry value fails to dispose. Unclassified native errors receive this code; * multiple failures expose an `AggregateError`, and existing foreign package identities remain. * * Inspect the original error, its `cause`, or each aggregate entry. Cleanup continues for other * owned values; retrying disposal does not rerun their callbacks.

members.name: providerRequired
members.description: A hook is called without `StoreProvider`. * * Wrap the subtree in `StoreProvider` or use a protocol hook that does not require a provider.

members.name: featureDisabled
members.description: An API requires a feature that is not explicitly enabled in the provider configuration. * * Enable that path in the `StoreProvider` `features` configuration.

members.name: storeMissing
members.description: The registry has no store for the requested token. * * Confirm that the store is registered and uses the same token.

members.name: storeDuplicate
members.description: The same token is registered twice. * * Remove duplicate registration or give each provider its own registry.

members.name: crossRuntime
members.description: A provider store belongs to another `Runtime`. * * Use the same `Runtime` for the store and registry. Cross-runtime injection is rejected.

members.name: invalidConfig
members.description: Provider or token configuration is invalid, for example a missing debug name or incompatible * `features.wasm` and `ready`. * * Correct the configuration before retrying. This is a permanent configuration error.

members.name: readyRejected
members.description: A non-Error readiness rejection is normalized before rendering can continue. Inspect `cause` * for the original reason; Error rejections, including frozen Errors, retain their identity * instead of receiving this code.

members.name: register
members.signature: register<T>(token: IStoreToken<T>, value: T, options?: IStoreRegistrationOptions): IDisposer;
members.description: Register one token, defaulting owned to false. Duplicate token, foreign Runtime ownership and closed-registry admission reject. The returned idempotent disposer removes only this entry; owned cleanup starts synchronously, with later rejection reported rather than awaited.

members.name: replace
members.signature: replace<T>(token: IStoreToken<T>, value: T, options?: IStoreRegistrationOptions): void;
members.description: Publish a new entry, defaulting owned to false, then release a different previously owned value. An old registration disposer cannot remove this replacement. Cleanup failure does not restore the old entry; asynchronous cleanup is reported and not added to whole-registry completion.

members.name: get
members.description: Read a registered value or undefined; use has to distinguish an explicitly registered undefined.

members.name: require
members.description: Read a registered value or throw STORE_MISSING; registry closure throws REGISTRY_DISPOSED.

members.name: has
members.description: Test exact token membership while open, without creating a reactive dependency.

members.name: remove
members.description: Remove a token and return whether it existed. By default start owned cleanup; false detaches without disposing. Later cleanup rejection is reported, not awaited by disposeAsync.

members.name: retain
members.description: Retain a committed Provider and return an idempotent release. If this release requests disposal and leaves no retainers, schedule a task to recheck the count/generation before disposing. A newer retain cancels that scheduled retirement, including StrictMode effect replay.

members.name: dispose
members.description: Idempotent, immediately enters `closing`. If an owned value's disposer returns a thenable, this cannot block on it (it's sync) — the thenable is tracked and observed (never left as an unhandled rejection) so a later `disposeAsync()` call still waits for it instead of resolving early just because `dispose()` already ran (see `disposeAsync()`). `lifecycle` only reaches `terminal` once every tracked thenable has actually settled.

members.name: disposeAsync
members.description: Awaitable counterpart. Single-flight: concurrent calls share one completion instead of each racing their own pass over `#entries`. Calling this after a prior synchronous `dispose()` does not resolve early — it waits for whatever thenable disposer results that `dispose()` started but could not block on (tracked by the lifecycle disposal ledger).

blocks.text: IStoreReadyBarrier 工厂为 `()=>Promise<unknown> 或 unknown`，归一化会同步调用它，结果用 Promise.resolve 接纳。所有屏障成功后渲染子树，任一失败在 render 抛给外层 Error Boundary；Provider 自己不提供错误 UI。Error 原因保持原实例（包括冻结 Error），非 Error 原因以 READY_REJECTED 包装并在 cause 保留，不进行字符串强制转换。features.wasm 的屏障可为任何等价初始化，不强制使用 store-wasm；ensureWasm 是可选组合。

同一 Provider/barrierScope、同一 ready 数组身份复用列表 Promise；新数组产生新就绪代，即使元素相同也重建 ReadyBoundary，旧代完成不能放行新代。工厂结果另按 scope+factory 身份缓存，在途/成功结果可跨列表复用，失败后删除工厂缓存，但同一旧数组仍复用已缓存的失败列表 Promise；单换数组不保证重新运行已成功的工厂。不同 Provider/请求 scope 隔离。abandoned render 之间不保证工厂恰好运行一次；非幂等初始化应由应用 owner 提供稳定 Promise。

已完成 Promise 的状态仍在 then 微任务更新，因此首次同步渲染可能 pending；客户端 effect 会重查，SSR renderToString 不运行 effect。保持 ready 数组、Store/Signal/Resource、selector/equality 身份稳定；配置是 readonly 输入，改变配置时提供新对象，不在 render 中写状态或创建持有资源的业务实例。

归一化配置的 features.wasm 为 boolean，features.experimental 为空原型浅冻结白名单，defaults 含 warnAsyncActions，ready 为 null 或带 promise/status()/error() 的跟踪对象；状态为 pending/ready/error；只有实验白名单被冻结，外层 features/defaults/ready 容器不保证冻结。StoreProviderState/IStoreProviderState 公开这三个值，状态不是错误码。实验键排序编码使输入键次序不影响配置；访问器不作为开启数据且不执行 getter，`__proto__` 是普通键。

rows: 返回当前 IStoreConfigValue，无 Provider 返回 null
path 为 `'wasm' 或 experimental.${string}`，无 Provider/未开启返回 false
apiName 默认 `'this API'`；无 Provider 为 PROVIDER_REQUIRED，未开启为 FEATURE_DISABLED
非 hook 查询，config 必填；未知路径或空实验键返回 false
非 hook 断言，可传 null，默认名同上
config 默认 undefined，scope 默认每次新 `{}`；显式稳定 scope 决定 ready 缓存隔离

blocks.text: IStoreReadyBarrier 工厂为 `()=>Promise<unknown> 或 unknown`，归一化会同步调用它，结果用 Promise.resolve 接纳。所有屏障成功后渲染子树，任一失败在 render 抛给外层 Error Boundary；Provider 自己不提供错误 UI。Error 原因保持原实例（包括冻结 Error），非 Error 原因以 READY_REJECTED 包装并在 cause 保留，不进行字符串强制转换。features.wasm 的屏障可为任何等价初始化，不强制使用 store-wasm；ensureWasm 是可选组合。

同一 Provider/barrierScope、同一 ready 数组身份复用列表 Promise；新数组产生新就绪代，即使元素相同也重建 ReadyBoundary，旧代完成不能放行新代。工厂结果另按 scope+factory 身份缓存，在途/成功结果可跨列表复用，失败后删除工厂缓存，但同一旧数组仍复用已缓存的失败列表 Promise；单换数组不保证重新运行已成功的工厂。不同 Provider/请求 scope 隔离。abandoned render 之间不保证工厂恰好运行一次；非幂等初始化应由应用 owner 提供稳定 Promise。

已完成 Promise 的状态仍在 then 微任务更新，因此首次同步渲染可能 pending；客户端 effect 会重查，SSR renderToString 不运行 effect。保持 ready 数组、Store/Signal/Resource、selector/equality 身份稳定；配置是 readonly 输入，改变配置时提供新对象，不在 render 中写状态或创建持有资源的业务实例。

归一化配置的 features.wasm 为 boolean，features.experimental 为空原型浅冻结白名单，defaults 含 warnAsyncActions，ready 为 null 或带 promise/status()/error() 的跟踪对象；状态为 pending/ready/error；只有实验白名单被冻结，外层 features/defaults/ready 容器不保证冻结。StoreProviderState/IStoreProviderState 公开这三个值，状态不是错误码。实验键排序编码使输入键次序不影响配置；访问器不作为开启数据且不执行 getter，`__proto__` 是普通键。

同一 Provider/barrierScope、同一 ready 数组身份复用列表 Promise；新数组产生新就绪代，即使元素相同也重建 ReadyBoundary，旧代完成不能放行新代。工厂结果另按 scope+factory 身份缓存，在途/成功结果可跨列表复用，失败后删除工厂缓存，但同一旧数组仍复用已缓存的失败列表 Promise；单换数组不保证重新运行已成功的工厂。不同 Provider/请求 scope 隔离。abandoned render 之间不保证工厂恰好运行一次；非幂等初始化应由应用 owner 提供稳定 Promise。

已完成 Promise 的状态仍在 then 微任务更新，因此首次同步渲染可能 pending；客户端 effect 会重查，SSR renderToString 不运行 effect。保持 ready 数组、Store/Signal/Resource、selector/equality 身份稳定；配置是 readonly 输入，改变配置时提供新对象，不在 render 中写状态或创建持有资源的业务实例。

归一化配置的 features.wasm 为 boolean，features.experimental 为空原型浅冻结白名单，defaults 含 warnAsyncActions，ready 为 null 或带 promise/status()/error() 的跟踪对象；状态为 pending/ready/error；只有实验白名单被冻结，外层 features/defaults/ready 容器不保证冻结。StoreProviderState/IStoreProviderState 公开这三个值，状态不是错误码。实验键排序编码使输入键次序不影响配置；访问器不作为开启数据且不执行 getter，`__proto__` 是普通键。

path 为 `'wasm' 或 experimental.${string}`，无 Provider/未开启返回 false
apiName 默认 `'this API'`；无 Provider 为 PROVIDER_REQUIRED，未开启为 FEATURE_DISABLED
非 hook 查询，config 必填；未知路径或空实验键返回 false
非 hook 断言，可传 null，默认名同上
config 默认 undefined，scope 默认每次新 `{}`；显式稳定 scope 决定 ready 缓存隔离

blocks.text: 本包校验通常保留 `RangeError`，释放、争用和缺少 waitAsync 使用 `Error`。未编码、可附码的 native updater Error 原位得到 `UPDATE_FAILED`，不替换原对象或 stack；冻结错误和非 Error 抛出值保留在包装错误的 `cause` 上。已有完整 foreign `source/code` 的错误保留其原 owner 和身份，因此不能假设每个 updater 失败都带本包 source。

`createStoreSharedError(code, message, options?)` 与 `createStoreSharedRangeError(code, message, options?)` 分别构造带身份的 Error、RangeError，供上层组合复用。两者 `code: IStoreSharedErrorCode` 和 `message: string` 必填，无默认；`options?: { readonly cause?: unknown }` 可选，无默认。仅当 cause 不为 undefined 时传入原 cause，再通过 `attachErrorIdentity` 附加 source/code，不重写 stack。

symbols.name: sharedInt32
symbols.purpose: Creates or attaches a current-ABI shared scalar with independent local Runtime observation state. New buffers initialize once; supplied buffers preserve their existing value and must match the current scalar ABI.
symbols.core:
runtime: Required IRuntime from directly installed @migaia/reactive createRuntime. It owns tracking, effect scheduling and watch error reporting; this package does not change its scheduler. Some examples explicitly select reactive schedulerStrategy for synchronous presentation.
initialValue: Optional signed int32 initial value, default zero; ignored when a buffer is supplied.
buffer: Optional current-ABI SharedArrayBuffer from another signal.buffer; default allocates 32 bytes. Old layouts or nonshared buffers reject rather than being reinterpreted.
SharedInt32Signal owned by the caller. Invalid shape/value/header uses INVALID_OPTION; short buffers use BUFFER_TOO_SMALL; contention uses CONTENTION_LIMIT. Dispose only this local wrapper.
parameters: This const declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this const.
examples:
import { createRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'
import { sharedInt32 } from '@migaia/store-shared'

const writer = sharedInt32(createRuntime(), 7)
const reader = sharedInt32(createRuntime(), 999, writer.buffer)
console.log(reader.peek())
writer.value = 9
console.log(reader.peek(), reader.isStale())

members.description: Runtime that owns this wrapper, its lazily materialized cells and watch diagnostics.

members.name: buffer
members.description: Shared ABI storage; attach another wrapper with the same length to share these cells.

members.name: length
members.description: Fixed number of int32 cells, including zero; it cannot be resized through this wrapper.

members.name: disposed
members.description: Whether this local wrapper has been disposed; metadata remains readable afterward.

members.name: get
members.description: Reads one consistent cell. Inside a reactive computation it lazily materializes that index's source, reconciles its version and tracks it; outside tracking it reads without a cell or graph publication. Throws ARRAY_DISPOSED, INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE or CONTENTION_LIMIT when applicable.

members.name: set
members.description: Writes an int32 cell, publishes its shared generation and notifies only its existing local index observers. An equal value is a no-op. Throws ARRAY_DISPOSED, INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, INVALID_OPTION or CONTENTION_LIMIT; local graph failure can occur after the write committed.

members.name: update
members.signature: update(index: number, update: (current: number) => number): number;
members.description: Reads, updates, and writes one cell. The callback runs outside the lock so a thrown exception cannot leave readers spinning on an odd locked version. The operation reads a consistent value, computes outside the lock, and writes with that value as its expectation. It retries if another writer changes the value. The `update` callback must be pure and repeatable. Avoid telemetry, requests, and irreversible side effects in the callback. Returns the committed value, or the observed value if unchanged. Invalid indexes/results throw INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE/INVALID_OPTION, disposal throws ARRAY_DISPOSED and exhausted retries throw CONTENTION_LIMIT. Callback errors keep a complete foreign identity; unclassified extensible native errors receive UPDATE_FAILED in place, while other thrown values remain reachable through cause. A callback failure itself never leaves the write lock held.

members.name: sync
members.description: Scans remote writes and notifies only affected index observers. An active `watch()` loop performs this automatically. Without `Atomics.waitAsync`, callers can poll from their message loop. Omitting index compares the shared generation, returning zero without a scan when unchanged, otherwise scanning all cells in one Runtime batch. The returned count includes changed cells without observers; each wrapper consumes only its own cursor. A supplied index checks only that cell and returns zero or one. Throws ARRAY_DISPOSED, INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE for an invalid supplied index, or CONTENTION_LIMIT for an unsettled cell.

members.name: watch
members.description: Starts an `Atomics.waitAsync` loop for the whole array. It waits on the generation epoch instead of creating a waiter for every cell. After waking, sync() scans cells and notifies observers only for cells that changed. The first call also reconciles missed writes synchronously. scheduler defaults to systemScheduler for zero-delay rearming; an active loop retains the first scheduler and returns the same stop function on repeated calls. Stop is idempotent and a later watch() can start a new loop. Throws ARRAY_DISPOSED after disposal or ENV_UNSUPPORTED without waitAsync; there is no silent polling fallback. Loop failures are reported through this Runtime, and dispose() also stops the loop.

members.name: snapshot
members.description: Copies all current values into a new ordinary Int32Array without tracking or publishing. Each cell is read consistently, but concurrent writes can occur between cells: the result is not an atomic whole-array snapshot. Mutating the copy cannot alter shared storage. Throws ARRAY_DISPOSED after disposal or CONTENTION_LIMIT if a cell cannot settle.

members.name: dispose
members.description: Idempotently stops this local watcher and disconnects all materialized index sources. Dispose dependent effects first if they would reread during disconnection. High-level reads, writes, synchronization and watch calls then throw ARRAY_DISPOSED; shared bytes and other wrappers are unaffected. Low-level cell primitives do not perform this lifecycle check automatically.

members.name: assertActive
members.description: Throws ARRAY_DISPOSED when composing low-level operations on a closed wrapper.

members.name: readCell
members.signature: readCell(index: number): { /** The cell's int32 value in this completed shared read. */ readonly value: number; /** Even shared seqlock sequence for that value, distinct from a local graph version. */ readonly version: bigint; };
members.description: Reads one cell consistently, returning a value and shared bigint version from the same observation. Extension code must supply a valid index and enforce the lifecycle itself; this primitive neither validates them nor tracks or publishes. Contention can throw CONTENTION_LIMIT. Prefer get() for checked application reads.
members.returns: { /** The cell's int32 value in this completed shared read. */ readonly value: number; /** Even shared seqlock sequence for that value, distinct from a local graph version. */ readonly version: bigint; }

members.name: writeCell
members.signature: writeCell(index: number, value: number, expected?: number): bigint | undefined;
members.description: Writes one cell and returns its new version. Returns `undefined` when the value is unchanged or the expected value does not match. Omitting expected means an unconditional write. The caller owns active/index/int32 validation and publication: after a changed write, call notifyWaiters() then sync(index) to notify an existing local source. This primitive does not do either step or advance observed cursors. Lock contention can throw CONTENTION_LIMIT; prefer set()/update() unless composing that complete protocol.

members.name: notifyWaiters
members.description: Advances the shared 64-bit generation and wakes array watchers after a low-level committed write. It neither publishes local sources nor consumes this reader's cursor; use sync(index) afterward for local publication. Extension code owns lifecycle checks and must not use this as a replacement for actually committing a cell write.

members.name: recordObservedVersion
members.description: Copies one cell version into this reader's array-level cursor without validation or graph publication. It is a bookkeeping primitive for extension code that already published the change; copying it before sync(index) would hide that change from the existing local source. Ordinary low-level writes should use notifyWaiters() then sync(index) instead.

runtime: Exact external Runtime supplied at construction, never transferred to another Runtime after creation.
buffer: Underlying SharedArrayBuffer issued by this constructor or attached from another instance.buffer. Share the buffer with another wrapper using the same kind and array length.
disposed: Local wrapper terminal state; disposal disconnects this Runtime only and leaves other wrappers sharing the buffer alive.
watch: Starts one Atomics.waitAsync wake loop that reconciles remote changes before each wait. It captures the expected version before sync, so a write during sync cannot become an unseen baseline. The stop handle is published before reconciliation, allowing reentrant stop/dispose. Active repeated calls retain the first scheduler and stop handle; no silent polling fallback is installed.
watch.scheduler: Optional IScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler; defaults to systemScheduler and controls zero-delay rescheduling and cancellation between wakeups.
No-argument idempotent IDisposer. Missing waitAsync throws ENV_UNSUPPORTED; asynchronous loop failures are reported to Runtime. Disposing the instance also stops its loop without deleting shared memory.
length: Application-selected fixed cell count, copied into the ABI header and checked on attachment.
get: Reads a validated cell; inside Runtime tracking it materializes or reuses only that index source, otherwise it reads directly.
get.index: Zero-based integer selected by the caller within zero inclusive and array.length exclusive.
Current consistent int32 value; invalid index uses INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, disposed access ARRAY_DISPOSED.
set: Writes a validated int32 and publishes only if its value changes; observers of other indices are not invalidated.
set.index: Zero-based integer selected by the caller within zero inclusive and array.length exclusive.
set.value: Caller integer in the signed int32 range, from -2147483648 through 2147483647.
No result; local cell tracking and shared generation publication are handled for this write.
update: Reads consistently, executes the callback outside the lock and attempts expected-value commit, retrying when a writer wins. User code never runs while the seqlock is held.
update.index: Zero-based integer selected by the caller within zero inclusive and array.length exclusive.
update.update: Synchronous current-to-next int32 callback, pure and repeatable because contention can invoke it again. Return a valid integer. It runs outside the lock; thrown native errors retain identity/class/stack with UPDATE_FAILED when unclassified, complete foreign identities remain unchanged, and other failures remain on cause.
Committed next integer or unchanged current integer; retry exhaustion uses CONTENTION_LIMIT, invalid output INVALID_OPTION.
sync: Publishes unseen remote cell versions locally. With an index checks one cell; without one scans only after the shared generation changes, batching notifications.
sync.index: Optional valid index; defaults to all cells after the generation gate.
Changed cell count; indexed calls return zero or one. Every wrapper owns its cursor, so one reader cannot consume another reader update.
snapshot: Allocates a nonshared Int32Array and consistently reads each cell into it. Concurrent writers may change other cells between reads, so this is not an atomic whole-array transaction.
New independently owned Int32Array with the observed cell values; contention or disposed access can reject.
dispose: Idempotently stops its watcher and disposes all materialized local index sources, preserving shared backing and other readers.
No result; validated public operations subsequently reject ARRAY_DISPOSED.
assertActive: Explicit local lifetime check for composition callers; does not read or synchronize shared cells.
No result while active; ARRAY_DISPOSED after disposal.
readCell: Low-level consistent value/version read without public index, active checks or graph tracking. Use get for validated application access.
readCell.index: Zero-based integer selected by the caller within zero inclusive and array.length exclusive.
{ value: number, version: bigint } from one stable cell observation; native indexing or contention failures can propagate.
writeCell: Low-level expected-value seqlock write without public int32, index or lifetime checks. Pair with notifyWaiters and local sync for publication; ordinary callers should use set or update.
writeCell.index: Zero-based integer selected by the caller within zero inclusive and array.length exclusive.
writeCell.value: Caller integer in the signed int32 range, from -2147483648 through 2147483647.
writeCell.expected: Optional expected current int32 from readCell; defaults to unconditional write. A mismatching expectation performs no commit.
New bigint version after a changed commit, or undefined for unchanged value or expectation mismatch. No notifications are published by this method alone.
notifyWaiters: Advances the shared 64-bit generation and wakes independent array waiters without advancing this reader full-scan cursor. Pair writeCell with notifyWaiters then sync(index); sync publishes existing local cells and manages their cursor, so no manual recordObservedVersion is needed.
No result; remote watch loops can now pull the new generation.
recordObservedVersion: Updates this array local cursor only; composition callers use it after their own notification path. It neither changes shared data nor emits graph notifications.
recordObservedVersion.index: Zero-based integer selected by the caller within zero inclusive and array.length exclusive.
recordObservedVersion.version: Exact bigint version returned by readCell or a successful writeCell commit.
No result; later array-level sync compares against the supplied cursor.
buffer: Optional buffer from another SharedInt32Array with identical length and current ABI header. Attaching never overwrites existing values or consumes initialValues.
Allocates a new SharedArrayBuffer for this fixed length, header and aligned 64-bit versions.
initialValues: Caller-provided iterable of signed int32 values, consumed only for a new buffer and only through the required length prefix. Zero length does not pull the iterator. Reaching the prefix closes the iterator through native IteratorClose without reading one extra item; iteration failures become native RangeError INVALID_OPTION with the original cause.
Omitted; new cells contain zero. Not consumed when attaching a buffer.

members.name: runtime
members.description: Runtime whose graph tracks this wrapper and receives watch-loop diagnostics.

members.name: buffer
members.description: Shared ABI storage to pass to another wrapper; disposing this wrapper does not erase it.

members.name: subs
members.description: Live read-only subscription view maintained by the Runtime; consumers must not mutate it.

members.name: version
members.description: Local reactive graph version, distinct from the shared 64-bit seqlock version.

members.name: disposed
members.description: Whether this local wrapper has been disposed; reading this flag remains valid afterward.

members.name: value
members.description: Reads a consistent shared value, publishes a newly observed remote version and tracks this source in the current reactive computation. Synchronous publication may itself change the value, so the returned value is reread after publication. Throws SIGNAL_DISPOSED after disposal or CONTENTION_LIMIT if a consistent shared read cannot complete.

members.name: value
members.description: Commits an int32 value, wakes remote waiters and notifies local graph observers. An unchanged value does none of these. Invalid values throw INVALID_OPTION; disposal and sustained lock contention throw SIGNAL_DISPOSED and CONTENTION_LIMIT respectively. Graph notification can fail after the shared write and remote wakeup have already committed.

members.name: sync
members.description: Pulls remote writes into this `Runtime`. An active `watch()` loop performs this automatically. Without `Atomics.waitAsync`, callers can poll from their own message loop. Returns true when this reader's observed shared version changes, false otherwise; it does not track a dependency. Throws SIGNAL_DISPOSED after disposal or CONTENTION_LIMIT when the shared read remains unstable.

members.name: watch
members.description: Starts an `Atomics.waitAsync` loop that publishes remote writes to this `Runtime` without manual `sync()` polling. The first call also reconciles existing remote writes synchronously. Its optional scheduler defaults to systemScheduler and owns zero-delay rearming, not the native wait itself. Repeated calls while active return the same stop function and retain that scheduler. Stop is idempotent, wakes a pending waiter and permits a later watch() to start a new loop; dispose() stops it too. Throws ENV_UNSUPPORTED without waitAsync or SIGNAL_DISPOSED after disposal. Loop failures go to runtime.reportError; ordinary sync() polling remains available without waitAsync.

members.name: peek
members.description: Reads current shared bytes consistently without tracking, advancing the observed cursor or notifying observers. A remote value can therefore be visible here while isStale() stays true. Throws SIGNAL_DISPOSED after disposal or CONTENTION_LIMIT when the read cannot settle.

members.name: onObserved
members.description: Reactive observation hook; this signal keeps its resources independent of subscriber count.

members.name: onUnobserved
members.description: Reactive unsubscription hook; it does not stop an explicitly owned watch loop.

members.name: isStale
members.description: Compares the current shared version with this reader's observed version without publishing or tracking. It remains callable after disposal, but an unsettled read can throw CONTENTION_LIMIT.

members.name: dispose
members.description: Idempotently stops this wrapper's watcher and disconnects its reactive source. Dispose local effects first if they would otherwise reread the source while it disconnects. Shared storage and other wrappers remain usable; value, peek(), sync() and watch() now throw SIGNAL_DISPOSED.

signalDisposed: Signal value, peek, sync or watch uses a disposed local wrapper.
bufferTooSmall: An attached buffer cannot hold the current signal or array layout; allocate the correct kind and size.
indexOutOfRange: A validated array API receives a noninteger or out-of-range index.

symbols.name: createSSRRequestScope
symbols.purpose: Constructs a request scope with a new Runtime by default. Retain it through rendering, register objects created with scope.runtime, and await disposeAsync afterward. Install @migaia/store-light and @migaia/resource directly for the examples that import them.
symbols.core:
options: Optional ISSRRequestScopeOptions, defaults to {}. runtime reuses an existing Runtime; runtimeOptions constructs a new one, and the two fields cannot be combined. Supplying a shared Runtime does not isolate requests.
SSRRequestScope with separate store/resource key spaces. register/registerResource default to owned: true and require the exact scope Runtime; detach transfers cleanup to the caller. Dehydrate copies/freezes supported JSON data. The Resource example overrides its default ttl of Infinity with 60000 ms to keep its completed cache eligible; ttl is a Resource option, not a scope option.
runtime: Existing IRuntime from @migaia/reactive createRuntime, mutually exclusive with runtimeOptions. The scope claims its own instance, not exclusive ownership of that Runtime. Applications provide a distinct Runtime and scope per request when isolation is required.
Creates an isolated Runtime.
runtimeOptions: IRuntimeOptions forwarded to reactive createRuntime when runtime is absent; callback, adapter and scheduler contracts remain defined by reactive.
Reactive defaults: microtask flushing, default host adapter and 100 maxFlushPasses.
runtimeOptions.adapter: Host capabilities: `scheduleMicrotask`, `now` (monotonic time), `timestamp` (epoch time) and `reportError`. Each missing entry falls back to the default.
`queueMicrotask`, `performance.now()`, `Date.now()` and a reporter that does nothing.
runtimeOptions.onError: Receives errors that the runtime cannot throw to a caller (effect failures during an async flush, lifecycle hook failures, trace listener failures) with a `phase` context. Synchronous reporter failures and returned thenable rejections reach the shared utils host exception queue, without changing graph operations.
Not set: errors go to `adapter.reportError`.
Set it in every long-lived runtime. An automatic flush runs in a microtask, so a failing effect has no caller to throw to; without `onError` the default adapter drops the error and the page just stops updating. Read `context.phase` and `context.observer?.debugName` to see which effect failed.
runtimeOptions.onTrace: Receives every trace event from creation on, same as calling `subscribeTrace` immediately.
Not set: no trace events are produced unless `subscribeTrace` is used.
Use it while diagnosing why an effect reruns too often, or to feed a devtools panel from the first node on. `subscribeTrace` called later misses the events of nodes created before it; `onTrace` sees them all. Each event names nodes by `debugName`, so give the nodes you care about a name.
runtimeOptions.maxFlushPasses: Maximum runs of one effect within one flush. Exceeding it is treated as a self-triggering loop: the queue is cleared and `FLUSH_LOOP` is thrown with the dropped node names. Must be a positive integer.
`100` runs per effect per flush.
runtimeOptions.scheduleIdle: Schedules cleanup work, such as suspending computed values nobody observes. Use it to align cleanup with animation frames or idle callbacks.
Uses `adapter.scheduleMicrotask`.
Use it when many computed values lose their last observer at once, for example when a large list unmounts, and the cleanup should not compete with the next interaction. Passing `requestIdleCallback` moves that cleanup to idle time; reading the computed again before then simply keeps it alive.
runtimeOptions.schedulerStrategy: Decides when pending effects flush: receives a `flush` function and calls it when appropriate (for example in `requestAnimationFrame`). It must call synchronously or schedule; returning a thenable falls back to the safe default and reports `INVALID_OPTION`.
Merge all writes of the current task into one microtask flush.
parameters: options: ISSRRequestScopeOptions (optional)
symbols.returns: SSRRequestScope
examples:
import { createSSRRequestScope } from '@migaia/store-ssr'
import { createStore } from '@migaia/store-light'

const scope = createSSRRequestScope()
const cart = createStore({ count: 2 }, { runtime: scope.runtime })
scope.register('cart', cart)
const snapshot = scope.dehydrate()
cart.count = 3
console.log(snapshot.stores.cart?.count, cart.count)
console.log(Object.isFrozen(snapshot.stores.cart))
await scope.disposeAsync()
console.log(cart.$disposed)

symbols.core:
runtime: Existing IRuntime from @migaia/reactive createRuntime, mutually exclusive with runtimeOptions. The scope claims its own instance, not exclusive ownership of that Runtime. Applications provide a distinct Runtime and scope per request when isolation is required.
Creates an isolated Runtime.
runtimeOptions: IRuntimeOptions forwarded to reactive createRuntime when runtime is absent; callback, adapter and scheduler contracts remain defined by reactive.
Reactive defaults: microtask flushing, default host adapter and 100 maxFlushPasses.
runtimeOptions.adapter: Host capabilities: `scheduleMicrotask`, `now` (monotonic time), `timestamp` (epoch time) and `reportError`. Each missing entry falls back to the default.
`queueMicrotask`, `performance.now()`, `Date.now()` and a reporter that does nothing.
runtimeOptions.onError: Receives errors that the runtime cannot throw to a caller (effect failures during an async flush, lifecycle hook failures, trace listener failures) with a `phase` context. Synchronous reporter failures and returned thenable rejections reach the shared utils host exception queue, without changing graph operations.
Not set: errors go to `adapter.reportError`.
Set it in every long-lived runtime. An automatic flush runs in a microtask, so a failing effect has no caller to throw to; without `onError` the default adapter drops the error and the page just stops updating. Read `context.phase` and `context.observer?.debugName` to see which effect failed.
runtimeOptions.onTrace: Receives every trace event from creation on, same as calling `subscribeTrace` immediately.
Not set: no trace events are produced unless `subscribeTrace` is used.
Use it while diagnosing why an effect reruns too often, or to feed a devtools panel from the first node on. `subscribeTrace` called later misses the events of nodes created before it; `onTrace` sees them all. Each event names nodes by `debugName`, so give the nodes you care about a name.
runtimeOptions.maxFlushPasses: Maximum runs of one effect within one flush. Exceeding it is treated as a self-triggering loop: the queue is cleared and `FLUSH_LOOP` is thrown with the dropped node names. Must be a positive integer.
`100` runs per effect per flush.
runtimeOptions.scheduleIdle: Schedules cleanup work, such as suspending computed values nobody observes. Use it to align cleanup with animation frames or idle callbacks.
Uses `adapter.scheduleMicrotask`.
Use it when many computed values lose their last observer at once, for example when a large list unmounts, and the cleanup should not compete with the next interaction. Passing `requestIdleCallback` moves that cleanup to idle time; reading the computed again before then simply keeps it alive.

symbols.name: SSRRequestScope
symbols.purpose: Creates a request registry bound to one Runtime for Store and Resource registration, snapshot generation and deterministic cleanup; equivalent to createSSRRequestScope.
symbols.core:
New request-owned SSRRequestScope with empty registries and fixed Runtime; finish with disposeAsync. Invalid options or simultaneous runtime/runtimeOptions throw INVALID_OPTION before a usable scope is returned.
runtime: Runtime fixed at construction, identical to the owner of every registered object. Cleanup releases registered owned objects; the scope does not dispose the Runtime itself.
disposed: Terminal flag set before cleanup; later active operations fail SCOPE_DISPOSED.
register: Registers a same-Runtime store. Pending hydration runs before commit, followed by an active-state recheck. A hydration throw leaves the key free and retains pending data while the scope remains active; disposal clears pending data and rejects SCOPE_DISPOSED. Neither failure transfers candidate ownership. Duplicates fail INVALID_OPTION, other Runtime fails CROSS_RUNTIME.
register.key: Caller-stable nonempty string other than `__proto__`; store and resource keys use separate namespaces.
register.store: ISSRStore, normally @migaia/store-light createStore with scope.runtime.
register.options: Optional ISSRRegistrationOptions; default owned true.
Void; retains the exact store by key.
unregister: Removes store registration, then starts requested owned cleanup. Synchronous failure leaves the key removed; asynchronous errors are retained for disposeAsync.
unregister.key: Caller-stable nonempty string other than `__proto__`; store and resource keys use separate namespaces.
unregister.disposeOwned: Default true; false leaves removed store alive.
Whether key existed; synchronous cleanup errors propagate.
detach: Removes store registration without cleanup and transfers ownership to caller.
detach.key: Caller-stable nonempty string other than `__proto__`; store and resource keys use separate namespaces.
Exact ISSRStore or undefined.
registerResource: Registers a same-Runtime resource; pending hydration runs before commit and an active-state recheck. A thrown hydrate leaves the candidate unowned and retains pending data only while the scope stays active. Disposal clears pending data and rejects SCOPE_DISPOSED without admitting the candidate. Caller cleanup remains required. Duplicates fail INVALID_OPTION and mismatched owner fails CROSS_RUNTIME.
registerResource.key: Caller-stable nonempty string other than `__proto__`; store and resource keys use separate namespaces.
registerResource.resource: ISSRResource, normally @migaia/resource Resource constructed with scope.runtime.
registerResource.options: Optional registration policy, default owned true.
Void; retains resource until removal or disposal.
unregisterResource: Disposes requested owned resource before deleting its registration; synchronous disposal failure leaves registration present.
unregisterResource.key: Caller-stable nonempty string other than `__proto__`; store and resource keys use separate namespaces.
unregisterResource.disposeOwned: Default true; false skips cleanup.
Whether registration was removed; original cleanup errors propagate.
detachResource: Removes resource without disposing it; caller takes cleanup ownership.
detachResource.key: Caller-stable nonempty string other than `__proto__`; store and resource keys use separate namespaces.
Exact ISSRResource or undefined.
hydrate: Validates, then applies entries best-effort. Missing registrations become pending hydration; each call replaces pending maps. Successful changes remain applied if another entry fails. One failure is rethrown unchanged; several become HYDRATE_FAILED AggregateError.
hydrate.state: Version-1 ISSRState from deserializeSSRState or validated application data.
Void; no rollback protocol is provided.
dehydrate: Reads live registrations in key order. Store fields and resource data are validated, deeply copied and frozen; metadata is shallow copied. Disposed entries and resource snapshots returning undefined are omitted.
Frozen ISSRState; unsupported data fails SERIALIZE_UNSUPPORTED, entry access failures can become INVALID_SNAPSHOT with cause.
dehydrateTrusted: Skips nested validation, copying and freezing. Only outer records are frozen; entry data remains live. Pair with serializeTrustedSSRState immediately for known immutable JSON fixtures.
Branded ITrustedSSRState, not an immutable snapshot.
awaitResources: Waits in waterfall rounds, deduplicating last Promise identity per key. New retries/refetches participate. Getter failures and rejections become diagnostics. Continued new work after 64 rounds rejects RESOURCE_ROUND_LIMIT. Disposal returns already collected failures.
awaitResources.options: Optional IAwaitResourcesOptions, default empty with no deadline.
Promise of readonly ISSRResourceFailure entries. At timeout only still-pending Promises receive RESOURCE_TIMEOUT; fulfilled entries are omitted and rejected entries retain their original reason. A zero budget recognizes already-settled work without awaiting in-flight resources. Invalid options reject the Promise rather than throwing synchronously.
dehydrateAsync: Waits, reports each failure, then calls dehydrate. It does not independently remove failed keys; inclusion follows resource.dehydrate. Disposal during waiting makes final dehydration reject SCOPE_DISPOSED.
dehydrateAsync.options: Optional IDehydrateAsyncOptions, defaults to no deadline and Runtime reporting.
Promise<ISSRState>; diagnostic throws/rejections are reported best-effort and do not stop other reports. Returned reporter thenables are observed without awaiting.
dispose: Marks terminal, wakes waits and clears registrations/pending state, then starts all owned cleanup: resources before stores, reverse registration order per group. Idempotent; one failure does not prevent other cleanup.
Void without awaiting store cleanup. One synchronous failure is rethrown unchanged; several become SCOPE_DISPOSAL_FAILED AggregateError. Await disposeAsync for completion.
disposeAsync: Starts disposal if needed and awaits every tracked owned cleanup. Completion is published before synchronous cleanup callbacks, so reentrant calls from dispose or disposeAsync share the same Promise. It waits for the full cleanup set admitted by the synchronous start pass and replays failures; the Runtime itself is retained.
Stable Promise<void>; exact single retained failure or SCOPE_DISPOSAL_FAILED AggregateError for multiple failures.

members.name: disposed

members.name: register

members.description: Register a same-Runtime Store under a unique nonempty key other than **proto**. Ownership defaults to true. Pending hydration runs before commit; a hydration throw while the scope stays active leaves the key free and state retained. Reentrant scope closure rejects admission without taking candidate ownership. Invalid/duplicate keys, invalid ownership, closed scopes and cross-Runtime Stores fail with their corresponding SSR code.

members.name: unregister
members.description: Remove a Store, returning false when absent. disposeOwned defaults to true and starts cleanup only for owned entries; async cleanup is tracked for disposeAsync(). Removal precedes cleanup, so a thrown Store failure does not restore registration. Closed scopes throw SCOPE_DISPOSED.

members.name: detach
members.description: Remove a Store without cleanup and return its exact reference, or undefined when absent. The caller assumes later cleanup responsibility; closed scopes throw SCOPE_DISPOSED.

members.name: registerResource
members.signature: registerResource(key: string, resource: ISSRResource, options?: ISSRRegistrationOptions): void;
members.description: Register a same-Runtime resource with ownership defaulting to true. Store/resource keys use separate registries. Pending hydration runs before commit; a throw while the scope stays active leaves the key free and state retained. Reentrant scope closure rejects admission without taking candidate ownership. Invalid/duplicate keys, invalid ownership, closed scopes and cross-Runtime resources fail with their corresponding SSR code.

members.name: unregisterResource
members.description: Remove a resource, returning false when absent. disposeOwned defaults to true; owned cleanup runs before deletion, so a thrown cleanup leaves this registration present. Nonowned resources are only unregistered. Closed scopes throw SCOPE_DISPOSED.

members.name: detachResource
members.description: Remove a resource without cleanup and return its exact reference, or undefined when absent. The caller assumes later cleanup responsibility; closed scopes throw SCOPE_DISPOSED.

members.name: hydrate
members.description: Applies validated JSON state best-effort rather than atomically. A store or resource can reject its own hydration; every other entry is still attempted and failures are collected. The contracts provide no stage/commit/rollback protocol, so successful changes remain applied. Pending hydration records always reflect the entries actually consumed, including when a later entry fails. Callers must handle partial application rather than assume rollback. Each call replaces pending tables for unregistered keys. One hydration callback failure is rethrown by identity; several become HYDRATE_FAILED with ordered errors.

members.name: dehydrate
members.description: Copy/freeze JSON Store state and includable resource data, sorting keys and omitting disposed or valueless entries. Getters may execute. Unsupported values, cycles or depth/node limits fail with SERIALIZE_UNSUPPORTED; closed scopes throw SCOPE_DISPOSED. No HTML encoding or waiting occurs.

members.name: dehydrateTrusted
members.description: Returns live business references without copying, deep-freezing or validation. Outer state and registration maps are shallow-frozen; later mutations to retained business values can change the payload before serialization, including across an await; this is not a snapshot. Use only for known-safe JSON data that stays immutable through serialization, such as owned documentation/demo fixtures. Request input or concurrently mutable stores must use dehydrate() instead. Select this unchecked path only when skipping validation and copying is justified. The TypeScript brand is not runtime validation; closed scopes throw SCOPE_DISPOSED.

members.name: awaitResources
members.description: Waits for registered asynchronous resources in rounds and returns their failures. Callers can fail the page or refetch on the client. New waterfall registrations participate in later rounds. Promises are deduplicated by identity, so a new retry or refetch promise for the same key is awaited. One resource failure does not block other prefetches. Thrown promise getters and timeouts are included in the failure list. Disposal during the wait returns results already collected without marking remaining resources as failures. The timeout is one total budget, with no deadline by default; waiting observes late rejection but never aborts resource work. Nonconverging waterfalls reject RESOURCE_ROUND_LIMIT, invalid budgets reject INVALID_OPTION, and an already-closed scope rejects SCOPE_DISPOSED.

members.name: dehydrateAsync
members.description: Takes a snapshot after prefetching. Each resource decides inclusion through its own dehydrate() result; the failure list does not independently filter payload keys. Reports failures to the runtime's `onError` with phase `ssr-resource` by default, so client refetches remain diagnosable. When `onResourceError` is provided, it handles reporting instead. Resource failures do not independently remove payload keys: each resource decides inclusion. Disposal during waiting can make the final dehydrate() reject SCOPE_DISPOSED. Timeout options use awaitResources() semantics; returned state has not yet been HTML-encoded.

members.name: dispose
members.description: Close admission, interrupt waits, clear state and start owned cleanup once: resources in reverse registration order, then Stores in reverse order. Disposed/nonowned entries are skipped and the Runtime stays caller-owned. All cleanup is attempted before a sole sync failure is rethrown or several become SCOPE_DISPOSAL_FAILED. Async Store jobs are observed by disposeAsync(); repeated dispose() is a no-op.

members.name: disposeAsync
members.description: Awaitable teardown boundary for real Store Light instances whose `$dispose()` is asynchronous. Concurrent and repeated callers share the same completion and failure replay.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Creates a request registry bound to one Runtime for Store and Resource registration, snapshot generation and deterministic cleanup; equivalent to createSSRRequestScope.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import SSRRequestScope from @migaia/store-ssr, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use SSRRequestScope when its class contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when SSRRequestScope does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.content: Use a maintained class example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.content:
New request-owned SSRRequestScope with empty registries and fixed Runtime; finish with disposeAsync. Invalid options or simultaneous runtime/runtimeOptions throw INVALID_OPTION before a usable scope is returned.
runtime: Runtime fixed at construction, identical to the owner of every registered object. Cleanup releases registered owned objects; the scope does not dispose the Runtime itself.
disposed: Terminal flag set before cleanup; later active operations fail SCOPE_DISPOSED.
register: Registers a same-Runtime store. Pending hydration runs before commit, followed by an active-state recheck. A hydration throw leaves the key free and retains pending data while the scope remains active; disposal clears pending data and rejects SCOPE_DISPOSED. Neither failure transfers candidate ownership. Duplicates fail INVALID_OPTION, other Runtime fails CROSS_RUNTIME.
register.key: Caller-stable nonempty string other than `__proto__`; store and resource keys use separate namespaces.
register.store: ISSRStore, normally @migaia/store-light createStore with scope.runtime.
register.options: Optional ISSRRegistrationOptions; default owned true.
Void; retains the exact store by key.
unregister: Removes store registration, then starts requested owned cleanup. Synchronous failure leaves the key removed; asynchronous errors are retained for disposeAsync.
unregister.key: Caller-stable nonempty string other than `__proto__`; store and resource keys use separate namespaces.
unregister.disposeOwned: Default true; false leaves removed store alive.
Whether key existed; synchronous cleanup errors propagate.
detach: Removes store registration without cleanup and transfers ownership to caller.
detach.key: Caller-stable nonempty string other than `__proto__`; store and resource keys use separate namespaces.
Exact ISSRStore or undefined.
registerResource: Registers a same-Runtime resource; pending hydration runs before commit and an active-state recheck. A thrown hydrate leaves the candidate unowned and retains pending data only while the scope stays active. Disposal clears pending data and rejects SCOPE_DISPOSED without admitting the candidate. Caller cleanup remains required. Duplicates fail INVALID_OPTION and mismatched owner fails CROSS_RUNTIME.

registerResource.resource: ISSRResource, normally @migaia/resource Resource constructed with scope.runtime.
registerResource.options: Optional registration policy, default owned true.
Void; retains resource until removal or disposal.
unregisterResource: Disposes requested owned resource before deleting its registration; synchronous disposal failure leaves registration present.
unregisterResource.key: Caller-stable nonempty string other than `__proto__`; store and resource keys use separate namespaces.
unregisterResource.disposeOwned: Default true; false skips cleanup.
Whether registration was removed; original cleanup errors propagate.
detachResource: Removes resource without disposing it; caller takes cleanup ownership.
detachResource.key: Caller-stable nonempty string other than `__proto__`; store and resource keys use separate namespaces.
Exact ISSRResource or undefined.
hydrate: Validates, then applies entries best-effort. Missing registrations become pending hydration; each call replaces pending maps. Successful changes remain applied if another entry fails. One failure is rethrown unchanged; several become HYDRATE_FAILED AggregateError.
hydrate.state: Version-1 ISSRState from deserializeSSRState or validated application data.
Void; no rollback protocol is provided.
dehydrate: Reads live registrations in key order. Store fields and resource data are validated, deeply copied and frozen; metadata is shallow copied. Disposed entries and resource snapshots returning undefined are omitted.
Frozen ISSRState; unsupported data fails SERIALIZE_UNSUPPORTED, entry access failures can become INVALID_SNAPSHOT with cause.
dehydrateTrusted: Skips nested validation, copying and freezing. Only outer records are frozen; entry data remains live. Pair with serializeTrustedSSRState immediately for known immutable JSON fixtures.
Branded ITrustedSSRState, not an immutable snapshot.
awaitResources: Waits in waterfall rounds, deduplicating last Promise identity per key. New retries/refetches participate. Getter failures and rejections become diagnostics. Continued new work after 64 rounds rejects RESOURCE_ROUND_LIMIT. Disposal returns already collected failures.
awaitResources.options: Optional IAwaitResourcesOptions, default empty with no deadline.
Promise of readonly ISSRResourceFailure entries. At timeout only still-pending Promises receive RESOURCE_TIMEOUT; fulfilled entries are omitted and rejected entries retain their original reason. A zero budget recognizes already-settled work without awaiting in-flight resources. Invalid options reject the Promise rather than throwing synchronously.
dehydrateAsync: Waits, reports each failure, then calls dehydrate. It does not independently remove failed keys; inclusion follows resource.dehydrate. Disposal during waiting makes final dehydration reject SCOPE_DISPOSED.
dehydrateAsync.options: Optional IDehydrateAsyncOptions, defaults to no deadline and Runtime reporting.
Promise<ISSRState>; diagnostic throws/rejections are reported best-effort and do not stop other reports. Returned reporter thenables are observed without awaiting.
dispose: Marks terminal, wakes waits and clears registrations/pending state, then starts all owned cleanup: resources before stores, reverse registration order per group. Idempotent; one failure does not prevent other cleanup.
Void without awaiting store cleanup. One synchronous failure is rethrown unchanged; several become SCOPE_DISPOSAL_FAILED AggregateError. Await disposeAsync for completion.
disposeAsync: Starts disposal if needed and awaits every tracked owned cleanup. Completion is published before synchronous cleanup callbacks, so reentrant calls from dispose or disposeAsync share the same Promise. It waits for the full cleanup set admitted by the synchronous start pass and replays failures; the Runtime itself is retained.

Creates an isolated Runtime.

Reactive defaults: microtask flushing, default host adapter and 100 maxFlushPasses.

`queueMicrotask`, `performance.now()`, `Date.now()` and a reporter that does nothing.

Not set: no trace events are produced unless `subscribeTrace` is used.

`100` runs per effect per flush.
runtimeOptions.scheduleIdle: Schedules cleanup work, such as suspending computed values nobody observes. Use it to align cleanup with animation frames or idle callbacks.
Uses `adapter.scheduleMicrotask`.
Use it when many computed values lose their last observer at once, for example when a large list unmounts, and the cleanup should not compete with the next interaction. Passing `requestIdleCallback` moves that cleanup to idle time; reading the computed again before then simply keeps it alive.

declaredConfiguration.name: runtime
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional existing Runtime; sharing it does not create request isolation.

declaredConfiguration.name: runtimeOptions
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional new-Runtime configuration; supplying both this and runtime fails.

declaredConfiguration.name: runtimeOptions.adapter
declaredConfiguration.description: Injects host capabilities. Missing entries use `defaultRuntimeAdapter`.

declaredConfiguration.name: runtimeOptions.maxFlushPasses
declaredConfiguration.description: Maximum executions for one observer within one flush. The default is 100. Exceeding the limit * is treated as a self-triggering cycle and throws after clearing the queue. * * The limit is configurable scheduling policy, not a physical constant.

declaredConfiguration.name: runtimeOptions.scheduleIdle
declaredConfiguration.description: Schedules suspension of an unobserved `Computed`. Defaults to the adapter's * `scheduleMicrotask`. * * Suspension is cleanup, so its timing is separate from flushing. This configurable channel can * align cleanup with animation-frame or idle policies without requiring callers or tests to wait * for a hard-coded microtask.

declaredConfiguration.name: runtimeOptions.schedulerStrategy
declaredConfiguration.description: Selects flush timing at creation; the runtime does not expose strategy replacement.

symbols.name: array
symbols.purpose: Describes fixed zero-filled f64 elements with shared tracking buckets. Call array(length, granularity?); there is no item builder parameter or compatibility overload for the old argument order.
symbols.core:
length: Caller-selected safe integer from 0 through 536870911; immutable element count, invalid values fail RangeError INVALID_OPTION.
granularity: Caller positive safe integer indices per bucket, default 64; one tracks each index independently, larger buckets can invalidate peers.
Returns Store Light IFieldBuilder with FIELD_BUILDER true, mode StoreFieldMode.sync from @migaia/store-light and synchronous create(context). A sync-only annotation is typeof StoreFieldMode.sync, not the full IStoreFieldMode union that also permits async. After ensureWasm, pass it to createStore; Store Light supplies {runtime,signal,createSource} and owns the field. Creation before readiness fails NOT_INITIALIZED. An aborted context preserves an unclassified native reason in place with INIT_ABORTED, a complete foreign identity unchanged, or an untaggable reason on cause. Rollback preserves primary and cleanup failures. Direct create requires caller-owned disposal. Field exposes readonly length/disposed, idempotent dispose(): void, at(index): number, setAt(index,value): void, setRange(lo,hi,values): void, view(): Float64Array. Indices are safe integers in [0,length); reads track buckets. Writes require number, including NaN/infinities. Range is half-open [lo,hi); all ArrayLike length and element reads finish before writes, so a getter failure leaves memory unchanged. Unclassified native input errors receive INVALID_OPTION in place, foreign identities remain unchanged, and frozen/non-Error failures remain on cause. Changed buckets commit once each in a batch; each commit refreshes the current memory view after owner-triggered memory growth, with attempted memory rollback on failure. view returns an independent copy without tracking, never writeback. After disposal data operations fail FIELD_DISPOSED; sources release before allocation.

granularity: number (optional)

blocks.text: STORE_WASM_SOURCE 为 `'store.wasm'`，只标识本包创建的错误；已有外包身份保持原 owner。可附码 native 输入读取失败原位附 INVALID_OPTION，不可附码时用 cause/errors；不要把声明的原生 WASM pass-through 错误强制重包为普通 Error。

四个公开错误工厂 code:IStoreWasmErrorCode 与 message:string 必填。`createStoreWasmError(code,message,options?)` 返回 Error，`createStoreWasmTypeError(...)` 返回 TypeError，options 默认 undefined，仅 cause，值非 undefined 时转发；`createStoreWasmRangeError(code,message)` 无第三参；`createStoreWasmAggregateError(code,errors:readonly unknown[],message)` 保留每个原错。它们构造不自动 throw，附不可写 source/code，不改 stack。

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content: Returns Store Light IFieldBuilder with FIELD_BUILDER true, mode StoreFieldMode.sync from @migaia/store-light and synchronous create(context). A sync-only annotation is typeof StoreFieldMode.sync, not the full IStoreFieldMode union that also permits async. After ensureWasm, pass it to createStore; Store Light supplies {runtime,signal,createSource} and owns the field. Creation before readiness fails NOT_INITIALIZED. An aborted context preserves an unclassified native reason in place with INIT_ABORTED, a complete foreign identity unchanged, or an untaggable reason on cause. Rollback preserves primary and cleanup failures. Direct create requires caller-owned disposal. Field exposes value getter/setter, readonly observed/disposed and idempotent dispose(): void. Reading tracks its source; Object.is-equal writes do nothing. Memory growth refreshes backing views. Disposed value access fails FIELD_DISPOSED. Disposal marks terminal, removes reactive sources then frees allocation. Value is boolean; true encodes as one and false as zero. Other types throw TypeError INVALID_OPTION.

Native WebAssembly.CompileError, LinkError and RuntimeError cross unchanged without source/code as the registered native pass-through exception. examples:
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
import initWasm from '@migaia/wasm'
import { ensureWasm } from '@migaia/store-wasm'

const url = new URL('./wasm_provider_bg.wasm', import.meta.resolve('@migaia/wasm'))
await initWasm({ module_or_path: await readFile(url) })
const first = ensureWasm()
const second = ensureWasm()
console.log(first === second)
const memory = await first
console.log(memory instanceof WebAssembly.Memory)
console.log(first === ensureWasm())

symbols.name: StoreWasmErrorCode
symbols.purpose: Stable public construction, lifetime, memory and cleanup failure codes interpreted with source.
symbols.core:
notInitialized: Field creation ran before ensureWasm completed; await readiness first.
fieldDisposed: Disposed field is read or written; create another instance.
initAborted: Field context signal was already aborted. Native reason identity, class and stack remain; unclassified extensible errors receive this code in place, complete foreign identities keep their owner, and frozen/non-Error reasons remain on cause.
reservedFieldName: Record would shadow dispose/disposed lifecycle keys; rename the field.
allocationFailed: Allocation/pointer handshake, alignment or stored string length is invalid.
invalidOption: Invalid size, granularity, write type, string capacity, index or range.
cleanupFailed: Several cleanup failures or rollback requires an aggregate to retain its primary.
instancePoisoned: Earlier WebAssembly.RuntimeError poisoned the shared arena; cause is the first trap. Reload/restart; allocation retries cannot repair it.

members.name: notInitialized
members.description: Rejects synchronous field creation or allocation before `ensureWasm()` finishes, or after * initialization fails. First await `ensureWasm()`, or use the `StoreProvider` `ready` barrier to * finish initialization.

members.name: fieldDisposed
members.description: Rejects scalar/record value access and array data operations after field disposal. Create a new * field instead of reusing it; metadata such as disposed and fixed array length remains * readable.

members.name: initAborted
members.description: Reports field initialization cancelled through an AbortSignal. Preserve an unclassified native * reason by identity/class/stack; complete foreign identities remain with their owner, and other * reasons stay reachable through cause. Handle it as cooperative cancellation.

members.name: reservedFieldName
members.description: Rejects a `wasm.record` field named `dispose` or `disposed`. Choose a different field name.

members.name: allocationFailed
members.description: Reports no usable allocation id/pointer, failed array alignment, or corrupt stored string * length. Check allocation availability and memory integrity. Invalid requested sizes are * INVALID_OPTION rather than this allocation/memory failure.

members.name: invalidOption
members.description: Rejects invalid field construction or write arguments, including excessive length, invalid * `granularity`, out-of-range indices or ranges, or inaccessible ArrayLike length/items. Keep the * original read failure reachable. Correct the parameter instead of retrying the same invalid * input.

members.name: cleanupFailed
members.description: Reports multiple owned-resource cleanup failures during field release or construction rollback. * Inspect `AggregateError.errors`. It preserves all original cleanup failures in execution * order.

members.name: instancePoisoned
members.description: Rejects allocation after an arena export used by this package on the shared instance raised * `WebAssembly.RuntimeError` (a trap). A trap can leave the Rust arena borrow held, so every * later export would trap again; the instance is unusable for the rest of the page or process. * `cause` is the original trap. Reload the page or restart the process; retrying cannot succeed.

symbols.name: WorkerAdapter
symbols.purpose: Creates a main-side client that asynchronously initializes a canonical worker endpoint; requests await readiness automatically. Pair it with createWorkerHandler on the worker. It borrows the supplied Worker and never terminates it.
symbols.core:
port: IWorkerPort, normally a Worker created by the application; preserve its event-listener methods.
New WorkerAdapter with asynchronous endpoint initialization already started; request awaits it and dispose shares one cleanup Promise. Invalid option-object access throws INVALID_OPTION synchronously, while endpoint initialization failure is observed through request/dispose.
disposed: True after close/dispose starts, before asynchronous endpoint cleanup completes.
request: Waits readiness then sends one canonical call. Generics only type the result; no runtime schema check is added. Payload passes recursive portable conversion, with bytes encoded to base64url and class prototypes not preserved; use supported plain data.
request.payload: Caller Input consumed by worker compute; avoid cycles and reserved $worker envelope keys.
request.options: Options default to {}; signal defaults to undefined and controls cooperative request cancellation. Inputs are copied without detaching caller buffers.
Promise<Output>; closed adapter rejects ADAPTER_DISPOSED, endpoint/RPC/compute failures keep their canonical identity. Classify ordinary request cancellation with RPC_CORE_ERROR_SOURCE and RpcCoreErrorCode.cancelled, not the serializer REQUEST_ABORTED code. close alone does not cancel admitted requests.
close: Idempotently marks unavailable synchronously; does not release endpoint or terminate Worker.
Void; later request calls reject immediately.
dispose: Closes adapter, awaits readiness and closes endpoint; never terminates the borrowed Worker. Repeated calls return the same Promise.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
port: IWorkerPort, normally a Worker created by the application; preserve its event-listener methods.
New WorkerAdapter with asynchronous endpoint initialization already started; request awaits it and dispose shares one cleanup Promise. Invalid option-object access throws INVALID_OPTION synchronously, while endpoint initialization failure is observed through request/dispose.
disposed: True after close/dispose starts, before asynchronous endpoint cleanup completes.
request: Waits readiness then sends one canonical call. Generics only type the result; no runtime schema check is added. Payload passes recursive portable conversion, with bytes encoded to base64url and class prototypes not preserved; use supported plain data.
request.payload: Caller Input consumed by worker compute; avoid cycles and reserved $worker envelope keys.
request.options: Options default to {}; signal defaults to undefined and controls cooperative request cancellation. Inputs are copied without detaching caller buffers.
Promise<Output>; closed adapter rejects ADAPTER_DISPOSED, endpoint/RPC/compute failures keep their canonical identity. Classify ordinary request cancellation with RPC_CORE_ERROR_SOURCE and RpcCoreErrorCode.cancelled, not the serializer REQUEST_ABORTED code. close alone does not cancel admitted requests.
close: Idempotently marks unavailable synchronously; does not release endpoint or terminate Worker.
Void; later request calls reject immediately.
dispose: Closes adapter, awaits readiness and closes endpoint; never terminates the borrowed Worker. Repeated calls return the same Promise.
Stable Promise<void>; initialization/cleanup failures reject.
clientId: String assigned by the caller for this RPC endpoint identity; the worker-side helper targets main, so the usual supported pair uses that default. Distinct topology requires a matching peer configuration.
main, a fixed identity rather than a generated unique ID.
timeoutMs: Optional per-request millisecond timeout forwarded to the canonical RPC send operation by WorkerAdapter; RPC owns validation, cancellation and timeout errors.
undefined: no default request deadline is supplied.

postMessage.value: Original frame value supplied by the canonical worker transport; forward it unchanged to native postMessage rather than wrapping it as another application request.
postMessage.transfer: Optional native transfer list received from send options; omit for ordinary cloning.
Void after the host accepted the send; it does not mean peer computation completed.
start: Optional synchronous native MessagePort start operation borrowed from the supplied port. The canonical worker transport invokes it before installing its message listener; Worker-like ports without this method need no substitute.

addEventListener: Host installs a listener for message, error or messageerror; RPC owns subscriptions and dispatch. Do not steal a mutable onmessage slot for the main-side adapter.
addEventListener.type: Event name supplied by the RPC adapter: message, error or messageerror.
addEventListener.listener: Synchronous callback receiving an event-like object with data, origin, source and type as applicable; return void, and transport isolates listener failures.
Void after listener registration.
removeEventListener: Host removes the exact type/listener pair installed by the transport during endpoint cleanup.
removeEventListener.type: Previously registered event name from the transport.
removeEventListener.listener: Exact callback identity received during registration.
Void after listener removal; native cleanup failures reject endpoint disposal.
terminate: Optional synchronous no-argument host cleanup callback; called after endpoint cleanup only when terminateOnDispose is true, even if endpoint cleanup failed.
Void; a failure rejects disposal alone or joins CLEANUP_FAILED AggregateError.

export declare function createSupervisor<
  TSpec,
  THandle extends IUnitHandle<TExit>,
  TExit,
  TContext extends ILaunchContext = ILaunchContext,

  options: ISupervisorOptions<TSpec, THandle, TExit, TContext>,
